I spend every day fighting for the American people in the US Senate. But, with a Republican Senate majority that is complicit in Donald Trump’s abuses of power, these fights haven’t been easy.

But when we stand firm in our convictions, we can still deliver.

Thanks to Senate Democrats and the thousands of folks who called their Senators, **Democrats successfully blocked Republicans’ additional DHS funding.**

**Moving forward, ICE or DHS should not get another cent until we get serious reforms and accountability.**

This fight is not over. Republicans have demonstrated time and again their hesitance to hold Trump and his lawless administration accountable.

We will continue to stand strong until Election Day, but we must understand that our best shot at the accountability and reform that this moment requires is flipping the Senate this November.

The Permanent Campaign is brought to you today in partnership with
Conservative Innovation
Issue: 2/16/2026
* * *

Rubio Rallies West in Munich

Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a [landmark address](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0LGOtCAUBeCn0Q4DV0acguJv7OZvtzR4uTPeBMEA6j7-xn2E7U5zTr6cr9f8chw4fv67jSyePPvk57pScSc5rCvX4jBzZXRhoRkkDEKCUMMcw6xab9EPPbRklTEKRqONblf7eOplfBOSURIN9tDD-EStjUZ6k4GW7b0kQRkplXmobhgRNKjek1_o2atGy2P3rlLpMMVC-XSVT-IY051S7DBtbbBrrXtp-n8NTA1M13V17_Qd6bprWwPTnsKNLw1MKZIoFCtFJJGPhVMR2xEZV1F2IlxFppNcIC9qPra9iExeBI4k6MhppzZbv18cApfBNFp-Nsfh11H_cN1p4ScAAP__SaaBHg) at the Munich Security Conference on Saturday, calling on European allies to defend Western civilization alongside the United States. Rubio struck a confident but warmer tone than VP Vance's speech at last year's conference, earning a standing ovation from the audience. He warned against the "dangerous delusion" of unchecked globalism and called [mass migration](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckM2upCAQhZ9GdxhAR3TBYja969nO0pRQtpUgdKBaZu7T3-gj3F3lq5yfnL_P5QkUKL7-wIHWnbT45BfescCJ4HgnLuAyMTkIKy5a6lFILdS4xLCo1lvnx163aJUxSk9mMEO7W1DKaTdtszTSbNOwOqXnuXemV4NWbm7JXk5SKyOlMr9UN05OD1r1Hv2Kc6-aQX7eHhhL51IsmE9gOpFiTNeVYufS0Qa7M79L0_9u9KPRj1prt6V_EeslOy6ScvCNfuTPSkmsAQoXcUNRiff0YbGm7DEXsUFkKP9FhRyLOKAUcdAr32mC94zAGIuoWBhzFI5OCvR1v9ts_btSCFRG0wzydQCFuyH_YNTT6u8AAAD__-MYi2w) an existential threat to sovereign nations. Sen. Dave McCormick called it a [defining speech](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLHSnSAQRp9GOxxYFfwLijR2N21KB5f1uhMEB1CTt8_cPMLffc135sz59VpejgPH9093kMWbF5_8Uncq7iaHdedaHGaujC6stIAELSQIpZcYFtV6i1730JJVxiiYzGCGdrd6gtWbVY9fPayj2foNNzeSkg51r6axZfshSVBGSmVG1ekJYQDVe_IrffWqGeR1elepdJhioXy7yjdxjOmzUuwwHW2we61nafofDcwNzM_zdFv6E-n53I4G5nRy5BQbmAtFcSCmfDD-FoUwU3X5r8jXykkUqkVgunIhEV1NRWxXvTIJunI6SQQulWKbrT8fDoGLNs0g34fj8N-kfiPebeFfAAAA__9sA4I6) for America First foreign policy, writing that Rubio diagnosed Europe's decline and charted a path forward. ★★★
Democrats Force DHS Shutdown

The Department of Homeland Security entered a partial shutdown Saturday after [Senate Democrats blocked](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGunDAQRb8GOiN7IPZu4SIN3aZNiQZ7WKwYG9kDZP8-ItL7gdfd5lwdnd-v6YUhhvT-hRtZd4bJZz_xShVPQsdr4IquBA4O40wTSNBCglB6SnFSrbfO6x5assoYBQ8zmKFd7aznp0HQ8NTYq0VqZwxoQEc9KNX7Ntj7SYIyUirzQ3X64WAA1XvyMz171Qzy2D0y1c7lVKmcyOGkkFK-V06dy1sb7cq816b_2cDYwHhdV7fkv4muG9saGPccb_nawLgQM5UNk5gP96cKT1t2BbmKip8qdiz8EfvB4osR-aQiXD4Sl4_waxV1PdjnK4nKmHxelrZYv18hxlC1aQb53jDE_2r8jZqnhX8BAAD__yJEiKE) a full-year funding bill already passed by the House on a bipartisan vote. Democrats are demanding [sweeping restrictions](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLHOpCAUhZ9GOwxcGXUKim3sZtstDXIvQoIXI4zu429m9g3-7ktOcnLO9-e1vGxMkbffdifjrrhgxqUGKvYi62qItVh3xhqdTSstIGEQEoQaFk6LatE4HHpoyahxVDCNetRtMKQUTE4OtLpJg7JP0DCoR6_dc_UefRvNp0mCGqVU40N1w-RAg-qRcKVnrxot3wfaSqVzmQudl63xosicP5S5c3lvkwm1HqXpfzUwNzDf9935_PeB7hM3MDPdpYF5yxedvBNXUcK7Yr5ZfK9wFi6RPcVhaxDEGHkTGIrw7_9cqmXM3renweOOKcUyjI2W225j-m6oP9B2GfgXAAD__2ahfiE) on ICE enforcement operations as a condition for restoring funding. Sen. John Fetterman was the only Democrat to break ranks and vote with Republicans, accusing his own party of putting politics over country. While ICE and CBP operations continue thanks to billions secured through last year's [One Big Beautiful Bill](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0L2u3CAQBeCnwR0WDF6zKVykcXfTprT4mV1GwWAx2Fd5-2i32jrdFKPv6JzfX9uXo0zl-cvtuISLtljj1hOyu9CFnqizC406BZc9bqBglgqknreSNz3EJcTZwICLtlbD3U52GtLiZwzgjQFljY_e-7v3E8DN3tBM3twHWl6SAm2V0vamx_keYAJtIkaPP4wWkzqP6DryGGphbJfrdCGVUl9XLWOo-5CX1PvBwvwUsApYU90xuxLHVE_G8VkvAesrScCqQMCqzceXZAxno_5XuuNo9Wj0llk2PE6fKbjCkrPbZcS9huY6y5hYcjp7rN9FPmqTjfgPladk98CX9MnWh3Q7tjckYB3aEo9vypl4tmJSz91Rfvfo_zH9tcC_AAAA__9ifZcF), agencies like TSA, FEMA, and the Coast Guard bear the brunt of the shutdown. Congress is on recess until Feb. 23, with no deal in sight. ★★★
Board of Peace Secures Billions

President Trump announced Sunday that members of his Board of Peace have pledged more than $5 billion toward humanitarian and reconstruction efforts in Gaza ahead of the body's [inaugural meeting Thursday](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOpDAQRL8GMiO3AXsmcHAJ2Vx6IWraPWDJ2Bb2wGm_fsV-wmYVVJWe3r_X_EIffFz_4s6WTj-75Oa6ccGTkerma0E6fPWEYeFZSaWFVAL0HMMMrbPkdK9atmAMqIcZzNButieDRKB7MwwEGp4AenxrI1GrfnxA6-39JBUYKcGM0OkHqUFB79gt_OyhGeQnO6xcOkqx8HFi9Sf7GNOdUuwo7W2wW625NP2fRk2Nmq7r6t7pf-Trnu2NmnIKN3xp1FSPz54Fxpg-kbiIUSw-BJ-iyIHdymLFLxTonVgSHk5kRmKx877wUdrDunzd_aJNM8h1Rx9-GOovtJ1WfQcAAP__30J93g) at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace in Washington. Member nations have also committed thousands of personnel to the International Stabilization Force. Indonesia confirmed up to 8,000 troops could be ready for [deployment by June](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0DEOnTAMxvHThC2IGF4CQ4YubK9rR2QSA5YgQUmAqqev6BG6efjL-un79Z2-yDuH9SceZN3Nk49-KhtlvAld2bhkdIkLO9xnmqABLRuQSk9hn1TlrfO6hYqsMkZBbzrTVZvVvUdnsKUBhsXgoJVG580yGzcrPywV2_dTA8o0jTIfVeveQQeq9eRnGloluuY6PRbKtYshU7qx8E0cQnyvGGoXj2q3WylnFu0PAaOA8Xme-sG8cVhLDPQbDw6U3lTAGOjJb7NxIbnFK5OAses-vYFewFjSdZxyjpi8jIs8CR3Jj5x53zkGueIflIleTEmXewkCxipZfz5vkrURXbMeyPs_WvmPNW8LfwMAAP__7qOGdw). More than 20 countries have joined the board, while Trump called on Hamas to uphold its commitment to [full demilitarization](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckDGO4zAMRU8jdwokWrKSQsU27rLtlgZNMTEBRTJsxYuZ0w-cI0xHgP_9B_x_9-mOkqU8_-KLIx0ypZqmtvCOByO1RdqOtEkTwjzzBAYGbUDbYSp5sl2KlIYeOo42BAvX4ILrltjPOFsfnKdHChRm8JYewRrq4ebQDZ3Es8mADcbY4O1luBI4sH3iNPOtt8qZ95qw8X6hWnbeDmxysJRSz6uWC9VXl-PS2rqr_o-CUcHYFl4k5_OnYFxrFvpSMEppvJUPhlnB6EN_81evvZ4lZ6lFP_Eb9canqm1vOpN6rrglXR96ZSRWMHZbTOv_k9iHoJx5vlA-rq79Yrojwk8AAAD__-oVfl0) under his 20-point peace plan.

Crypto PAC Drops $5M on Alabama Senate Race

The crypto-backed Defend American Jobs super PAC announced a $5 million spend to boost Trump-endorsed Rep. Barry Moore's Alabama Senate bid, as the Fairshake network's [$193 million war chest](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2u4yAQRp_G7hzB4IBdUGzjLttuaREYh5EwWDBxlLdf-T7C7b4f6RTn32N9OEqUX3_djtaftIYSVo7Y3InOcyRuzldi8i49cQUBehAwSL3mtMo-WB-0gh6tNEbCZEYz9tEGuekNR40bqjsYseE8q0lPmxv9DPPWk71IAqQRQpq7vOnJwwhSBQxPnJXsRvE-gmNsN19yw3o6phMp53Klkm--7H2ykflonfrTwdLBwhEjpXR9HSxHSeS_14w-5pLK6yp3oyYlpsHX78FloBzejet32Ckw1r0NH1cHH7FxB0tfbTg-lBI1bbpRvHZHP_ief2HrtPA_AAD__w_memg) targets key 2026 races.

★★★
Noem Champions Election Integrity for Midterms

DHS Secretary Kristi Noem declared elections "critical infrastructure" at an Arizona press conference, backing the SAVE Act and pledging to ensure the [midterm voting process](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0D3u3CAUBPDT4M4reGBYCoo07jZtSouFt-ZJfFiGeK8fOUf4dyON5lfMn9f28pSp7r99QRcu2mKL20jY_YU-jESj-3DSoODzGzfgoGcOs9BbzZuYogtRS5jQCWMEPI0yakouLEZ4_bHW6EVFK73SH6tUXKKVUsXPRO6WOAjDuTCLeOhnAAVCRoxvtFIwxf8e0Q_sj9Bqx_Pygy6kWtudWn2EVqbs0hhHZ_IXg5XBOhImyvnuGKypFaz47QzW4Mvhaa8M1sVIK-E514Zlvtqgus-F4sCzzJgx3Pg9mU4Xjy_lTF0bpvhePP2Xp_GDoy4H_wIAAP__27t3mQ) is secure for American citizens ahead of the November elections.

★★★
Trump Blasts NY/NJ Project

President Trump said Washington will pay [“not one dollar”](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0LEOpCAQxvGnwU4DgwtuQXEN3V57pRlhVidBNIJ69_YX7xGu-yWTTP75fn3GD3LiPP_ElVy4eIxbHOtCBS_CUBeuBcPBlQOmiUaQYFoJrTJjTqNqogvRaGjIKWsVDLa3fbM4HXoT9WAHmqR6o0QVwjRYa5SZNKp3w-75JEFZKZV9qc4MAXpQOlKc6K2V6OW5R6xUurDlQseFlS_inLdHW-7CtjbJLbXuRegfArwAf993l-kuK_5-7gL8WQT4epzr3s5Y6cY_7YGc2nrmTKn9UqQDU_s9c-Q8C_BPlwAvQYBXjzg-gt5o-RLgm8PF_eaUuBgrejmvyOlfTP2P_S4HfwMAAP__MoJ8rA) of Gateway Tunnel cost overruns, calling the NY/NJ project a potential boondoggle. He told Gov. Kathy Hochul and New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill that the states must cover any extra billions.

* * *

Hi Peter,
Last week we saw more than 200 wildlife advocates in the Capitol, to rally and meet with their legislators in support of the 1.25% for Wildlife bill ( HB 4134 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2026R1/Measures/Overview/HB4134] ). The support we have shown for this bill has been building since last session. It has just made it out of committee, so we are very close to getting it passed, as it is moving on to the House for a vote. Now is the time to show up more than ever! Will you send your message of support to your representatives? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/XQ3kk2F_m0-wtJXO_GbAkQ2]
Send your message [https://secure.ngpvan.com/XQ3kk2F_m0-wtJXO_GbAkQ2?contactdata=rkDiEQlRNtpGL10CwGmfx3d7ik4dIuACjesgpEKHT2itJPvRd+jI9zyJ5e03cQn8oSWbq/v/wln0I35LHtgk9MaeI6bhLAgJFuYTyTFRO8ElfRUL7pl857UJG5GQAaxw]
What would this bill do? 1.25% for Wildlife would secure landmark wildlife and habitat conservation funding by dedicating a small share of Oregon’s tourism lodging tax to our wildlife. Oregon’s lodging tax is currently one of the lowest in the country, and this increase will still keep it at one of the lowest levels, while providing our endangered wildlife with the support they desperately need.
Oregon’s wildlife is at a tipping point. 1.25% for Wildlife is our chance to make a real difference for Oregon’s endangered species.
Take action now and urge your representatives to vote YES on HB 4134! [https://secure.ngpvan.com/XQ3kk2F_m0-wtJXO_GbAkQ2]
Thank you for your support,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Eliza.png]
Eliza Walton (she/they)
OLCV Coalition Director

body:
I want to try something radical.

**I want to try something different.**
You probably get lots of fundraising requests from House and Senate campaigns that will cost tens of millions of dollars to win.
But what about the races where a fraction of those fundraising numbers can actually flip a seat? Let me explain:
This weekend I am going to Tennessee for the first stop on my book tour. While I am there, I'm hoping to meet with three candidates for the Tennessee House of Representatives who lost very close races last election.
Bryan Goldberg in TN-18 lost his race last cycle by 2,600 votes. The winner spent $150,000.
Allie Phillips in TN-75 lost her race by 2,000 votes, and her opponent spent around $200,000.
Jesse Huseth in TN-97 lost his race by 1,000 votes despite being outspent by $40,000.
Running for office as a Democrat in Tennessee can be a difficult decision; You put your name on the ballot knowing you'll be absolutely bombarded with attacks from the Republican Party. But if these three Democrats have the resources, they will win this November -- especially if we get that "blue wave" election.
By the time you are at this point in the email, lots and lots of people have added their donations to these candidates. We're tracking in real time. But now I am asking you to add one of your own.
So I am asking, humbly:
[**Please split a contribution of $3 or whatever you can afford between Bryan Goldberg, Allie Phillips, and Jesse Huseth running for the State House in Tennessee. name: Karl for Congress
subject: Things You Might Have Missed
body:
[](https://karlforcongress.us/updates/d5ab9094/)
---
While ICE, arrested journalists, and the Epstein Files have rightfully dominated recent headlines, there has been a lot of other news worth our attention as well. For instance, [the New York Times Editorial Board reported](https://link.karlforcongress.us/6993adb6/ "How Trump Has Pocketed $1,408,500,000") that Donald Trump has enriched himself to the tune of 1.4 billion dollars since retaking office. The lion's share of that newfound wealth came from his cryptocurrency operations, including the [sale of a 49% stake](https://link.karlforcongress.us/6993af0b/ "United Arab Emirates’ ‘Spy Sheikh’ bought secret stake in Trump crypto company: WSJ") of his crypto company, World Liberty Financial, to Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the National Security Advisor of the United Arab Emirates. Shortly after taking office, Trump lifted a ban on the sale of [AI chips to the UAE](https://link.karlforcongress.us/6993b6f6/ "U.S. approves sale of 70,000 AI chips to UAE and Saudi Arabia, WSJ reports"). I'm not sure how much clearer a bribe can be! The Trump family has been enriching itself through crypto for the past 2 years and Congress, as usual, has been slow to act. On the AI front, it is worth taking note of the AI researcher that resigned from Anthropic to move to the UK and "[become invisible](https://link.karlforcongress.us/6993ad2d/ "Anthropic AI Safety Researcher Warns Of World ‘In Peril’ In Resignation")." This is one of many resignations in recent weeks from top AI firms with many expressing displeasure or distrust in their companies, their roles, or their overall view of where AI is headed. Let me reiterate a point I made a few months ago: **this is a break-glass moment**! We need Congress to begin regulating this technology and ensuring guardrails are put in place, or we will soon get to a point of no return.
#### It's Petition Season
It's time for us to get petitions signed and submitted to Harrisburg to be on the ballot in May. If you are: **1)** a registered Democrat, and **2)** a Pennsylvania resident, and would like to help us cross the finish line by circulating a petition to your friends, family, and neighbors, [let us know](mailto:volunteer@karlforcongress.us "Volunteer to help get petitions signed"). We'll be in touch with all the information and resources you need.
#### Closing Out Black History Month in Style
On February 28th at 6 PM we'll be hosting a Black History Month Karaoke and Games event at the [Church of the Annunciation](https://maps.app.goo.gl/LFhRjYxwjrR5ZSMb9 "Church of the Annunciation") in West Mount Airy! You can [purchase tickets here](https://link.karlforcongress.us/karaoke "Purchase tickets for Karaoke"). Come out and let's end Black History Month with some fun and fellowship!
| _Your support is what makes this campaign possible.[Donating](https://link.karlforcongress.us/donate/ "Donate to the campaign") is the easiest way to help us bring our message of equal protections and benefits from emerging technologies to Washington!_

body:
This is exactly how we can tell that the party behind this change doesn't care about anything other than winning elections, Team.
That's because that same party once led the charge for widespread mail-in ballot use in the 90's -- in key states like Arizona, all in the name of democracy and the right to vote -- is strangely silent now that those same voters might be silenced by administrative mail delays.
Team, the MAGA movement and the party it has taken over won't stop until the only valid ballots being counted are their own. RUSH $35 or more right now to help us fight back and make sure every vote counts in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021626_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Fox 7 Austin: New Postal Service guidance on postmarks could affect ballot, tax deadlines [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021626_3&amount=25]
The day you mail something may no longer count as the actual mailing date, Team.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
USPS has now reversed that practice. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility, not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over.
What does this mean? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
Our first priority is making sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- not just in terms of vote-by-mail, but their bills, their taxes, responses to companies, you name it. What we all think is the deadline may not be the deadline and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media.
We also need to make sure every mail-in voter across the country knows how to get their ballot in on time, especially those most vulnerable to this change, like the elderly, rural Americans who live far from USPS regional facilities, our military service members, and young people who are voting by mail away from home.
Team, will you pitch in $35 or whatever you can today and help us spread the word about these changes so we can protect mail-in ballots? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021626_3&amount=35]

In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. Our first priority is making sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- not just in terms of vote-by-mail, but their bills, their taxes, responses to companies, you name it. What we all think is the deadline may not be the deadline and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media. We also need to make sure every mail-in voter across the country knows how to get their ballot in on time, especially those most vulnerable to this change, like the elderly, rural Americans who live far from USPS regional facilities, our military service members, and young people who are voting by mail away from home. | | | | | | Hi, Peter,Presidents’ Day was meant to honor leaders, like George Washington and Abraham Lincoln — people who believed in democracy, accountability, and a government of the people — and FDR, who believed in social safety nets and relief for people living in poverty. Today, those values feel under attack. Corruption, abuse of power, and fear politics are threatening the very foundations of our democracy. We are a nation built by immigrants and powered by everyday people — and we deserve leadership that reflects that truth.
_But it doesn’t have to be this way._
We can organize. We can vote. We can show up. We can spend our money and cast our ballots with intention. And we can elect leaders who refuse corporate checks and answer only to the people they serve.
That’s how I’ve run every one of my campaigns -****[**people-powered and unapologetically independent.**](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=2b0e0b70be&e=8249791cac) I can’t be bought by corporate interests.
If we work together, we can build a government our history would be proud of — and a future worthy of the next generation. [**Join me**](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=a758a84aa4&e=8249791cac)[**.**](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=f33c4832d6&e=8249791cac)
In solidarity,
**Brianna Titone**
Brianna for Colorado State Treasurer

_🔗**Learn more & join the campaign:**_[__](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=5984f90927&e=8249791cac)[_www.briannaforco.com_](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=092b33f696&e=8249791cac)

TOP NEWS " Southwest Airlines works to address issues with new assigned seating as customers fume" via - It's safe to say that Southwest Airlines ' transition to assigned seating is off to a turbulent start. Customers have taken to social media platforms for days to complain about things like lack of overhead bin space and not being allowed to switch seats, even when there are plenty open. Southwest, Love Field Airport's dominant carrier, began assigned seating on Jan. 27, ending its popular open seating policy. CEO Bob Jordan previously said that surveys conducted by Southwest showed customers and potential customers overwhelmingly wanted the option to pick their seat, similar to other major U.S. Airlines like Fort Worth-based American. The monumental switch was first announced in 2024. Around the same time, Southwest's management came under pressure following an activist takeover by Elliott Investment Management. () " American Airlines flight attendants vote no confidence in Isom as carrier underperforms" via - American Airlines' flight attendants have voted no confidence in the leadership of Robert Isom , the first time they have taken such an action against a sitting chief executive in its nearly 50-year history. The vote was unanimous amongst the board of directors for the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, the union that represents American's more than 28,000 flight attendants. It comes less than two weeks after the union called for new leadership. "From abysmal profits earned to operational failures that have front-line workers sleeping on floors, this airline must course-correct before it falls even further behind," said a statement from Julie Hedrick , president of the APFA. "This level of failure begins at the very top," she added. () " El Paso airspace closure was tied to Mexican cartel drones, White House official says" via - The Federal Aviation Administration reopened the airspace around El Paso International Airport in Texas on Wednesday morning, just hours after it announced a 10-day closure that would have grounded all flights to and from the airport. The Federal Aviation Administration said in a social media post that it has lifted the temporary closure of the airspace over El Paso, saying there was no threat to commercial aviation and that all flights will resume. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X that the FAA and the Defense Department "acted swiftly to address a cartel drone incursion. The threat has been neutralized and there is no danger to commercial travel in the region." He said normal flights are resuming Wednesday morning. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Attorney General Paxton, DOJ Announce $68 Million Settlement with Colony Ridge Developers" Meridith Dyer - Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , working with President Donald Trump 's Department of Justice (DOJ), announced a $68 million settlement against the developers of Colony Ridge. The settlement addresses a 2023 federal lawsuit brought by the DOJ and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and a 2024 lawsuit filed by the Texas Office of the Attorney General in federal court, both alleging deceptive lending and marketing practices. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " 5 council members seek formal reprimand over mayor's 'unprofessional conduct'" Andrea Drusch - Five members of the City Council are requesting a meeting to reprimand Gina Ortiz Jones over "repeated instances of unprofessional conduct." The move comes after Jones allegedly yelled at Sukh Kaur (D1) in a private meeting space last week, drawing a formal complaint from Kaur, and an investigation into whether the mayor violated the council's code of conduct. City Attorney Andy Segovia determined that outside counsel should look into the Feb. 5 incident, according to city spokesman Brian Chasnoff , and the City Council will receive a report once the investigation is complete. The council created a code of conduct in 2024 to address issues like inappropriate relationships with staff members, as well as set formal standards for how council members interact with one another and members of the public. () " Harris County to Provide Taxpayer-Funded Legal Assistance for H-1B Visa Applicants for County Jobs" Holly Hansen - Although Texas Gov. Greg Abbott ordered state agencies and universities to pause their use of a federal program that brings foreign workers to the country for specialized work amid allegations of fraud and abuse, Harris County will continue to use the program and provide some legal assistance to applicants. At the end of January, the Harris County Commissioners Court approved a contract as part of a consent agenda with Quan Law Firm to assist county employees with H-1B visa and Permanent Resident Card, also known as "Green Card," applicants. () " Transportation leaders support 'Hail Mary' plan to save DART, signaling election recalls" via - The Regional Transportation Council voted Thursday to commit funds to DART's plan to give some resources back to cities, a proposal some suburban leaders said could persuade them to cancel May elections on cutting ties with the public transportation agency. The 45-member transportation policy body of the North Central Texas Council of Governments approved committing $180 million to Dallas Area Rapid Transit, the Denton County Transportation Authority and the Trinity Railway Express. Of the commitment to regional transit, $75 million would go to DART's funding plan. Randall Bryant , DART Board Chair, presented the plan to the agency's board of directors Tuesday, a proposal to save the regional transit system as Plano, Irving, Farmers Branch, Addison, University Park and Highland Park -- six of DART's 13 member cities -- near a deadline to call off withdrawal elections. () " Fort Worth City Council hits 'pause' on $10 billion data center project" None - The developer of a planned $10 billion data center in southeast Fort Worth has hit a speed bump in the rezoning of land for what could become one of the largest data center campuses in the metroplex. Black Mountain, a Fort Worth-based energy consortium, has successfully petitioned the city to rezone roughly 431 acres of land in the southeast corner of the city near Forest Hill and Everman. At the Fort Worth City Council meeting Feb. 10, Black Mountain was scheduled to ask the city to rezone another roughly 80 acres of land in two separate requests. One of those requests is for about 42 acres on the east side of Anglin Drive near the Forest Hill city line. That request was rescheduled after leaders in nearby cities asked for a discussion with council member Chris Nettles , who represents that part of Fort Worth. The other request, for about 38 acres east of Anglin Drive and north of Everman Kennedale Road, was previously approved by the Zoning Commission. () 2026 " New Texas Primary Poll Shows Roy, Middleton Leading in Attorney General Race" Mary Elise O 'Bar - A new survey shows Congressman Chip Roy (R-TX-21) pulling ahead in the Texas attorney general race, while Texas comptroller candidate Don Huffines and incumbent Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller are similarly taking the lead in their Republican primary races. The poll, conducted by the University of Houston (UH) Hobby School of Public Affairs, collected responses from 550 likely voters in Texas for both the Republican and the Democratic primary elections, respectively, between January 20 and January 31. Both populations have a margin of error of +/- 4.18%. () " Democrats Running for Texas Attorney General Vow to Reform Office Post-Paxton" Holly Hansen - The open seat for Texas attorney general has drawn three candidates who are staking out positions in the runup to the March 2026 Democratic primary election by taking aim at the outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton, his potential Republican replacements, and, at times, each other. Democratic candidates running for attorney general this year are state Sen. Nathan Johnson (D-Dallas), former Galveston Mayor Joe Jaworski , and former Federal Bureau of Investigation agent Tony Box. During a recent forum attended only by Jaworski and Johnson, the candidates sparred over experience and whether a Democratic attorney general should work with Republicans in the state. "When you look at my opponent's record in the Senate, he is very comfortable cutting deals with [Lt. Gov.] Dan Patrick to keep his cherished committee vice chairmanship," said Jaworski. "That might be fine for the Senate, ladies and gentlemen, but it's not what we need in our lead attorney." () " Bexar County judge contenders rewrite history, talk over each other at fiery debate" Andrea Drusch - In a fiery one-hour debate Tuesday night, Bexar County Judge Peter Sakai and Democratic primary challenger Ron Nirenberg talked over one another, rewrote history on a major downtown development project and cast blame over who was at fault for a faltering relationship between city and county officials. The two men overlapped as top leaders of a blue city and county -- Nirenberg as San Antonio mayor and Sakai as Bexar County's top executive -- for two and a half years. Now opponents in a heated Democratic primary, they've gone deep into the weeds on past policy fights to differentiate themselves in a race where few ideological differences exist. "We may go back and forth, there may be a lot of words said," Sakai warned the crowd of more than 500 people at Stable Hall in his opening remarks. "But I'm asking you to look at who I am." Early voting for the March 3 primary starts on Feb. 17. () TEXANS IN DC " Roy's SAVE Act Requiring Proof of Citizenship for Federal Voter Eligibility Passes U.S. House" Mary Elise O 'Bar - Congressman Chip Roy 's (R-TX-21) legislation requiring proof of American citizenship to vote in federal elections passed the U.S. House on Wednesday, after similar versions passed the lower chamber twice in recent years before ultimately failing in the U.S. Senate. Known as the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) or SAVE America Act, the bill would amend the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) of 1993 by requiring states to verify U.S. citizenship and identity through documentary proof in person when an individual registers to vote in federal elections, regardless of the registration method. * **TOP NEWS**

**" Southwest Airlines works to address issues with new assigned seating as customers fume"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/759002a4-681f-426f-82ac-16b532b47ea7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - It's safe to say that **Southwest Airlines '** transition to assigned seating is off to a turbulent start.

Customers have taken to social media platforms for days to complain about things like lack of overhead bin space and not being allowed to switch seats, even when there are plenty open.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/cceb38f1-99c5-43bd-aae7-71d8f1fea1f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/cceb38f1-99c5-43bd-aae7-71d8f1fea1f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Southwest, Love Field Airport's dominant carrier, began assigned seating on Jan. 27, ending its popular open seating policy. CEO **Bob Jordan** previously said that surveys conducted by Southwest showed customers and potential customers overwhelmingly wanted the option to pick their seat, similar to other major U.S. Airlines like Fort Worth-based American.

The monumental switch was first announced in 2024. Around the same time, Southwest's management came under pressure following an activist takeover by Elliott Investment Management.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/9360da93-93cc-49d7-8f01-ff561d017a2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" American Airlines flight attendants vote no confidence in Isom as carrier underperforms"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/6f915ab8-d6df-45f8-949d-3f9137542160?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - American Airlines' flight attendants have voted no confidence in the leadership of **Robert Isom** , the first time they have taken such an action against a sitting chief executive in its nearly 50-year history.

The vote was unanimous amongst the board of directors for the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, the union that represents American's more than 28,000 flight attendants.

It comes less than two weeks after the union called for new leadership.

"From abysmal profits earned to operational failures that have front-line workers sleeping on floors, this airline must course-correct before it falls even further behind," said a statement from **Julie Hedrick** , president of the APFA.

"This level of failure begins at the very top," she added.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/d217fa48-bb1d-4273-95b5-2ec6850a9d67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" El Paso airspace closure was tied to Mexican cartel drones, White House official says"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/73d07467-101f-4a03-afb8-c76a9021423a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - The Federal Aviation Administration reopened the airspace around El Paso International Airport in Texas on Wednesday morning, just hours after it announced a 10-day closure that would have grounded all flights to and from the airport.

The Federal Aviation Administration said in a social media post that it has lifted the temporary closure of the airspace over El Paso, saying there was no threat to commercial aviation and that all flights will resume.
Transportation Secretary **Sean Duffy** said in a post on X that the FAA and the Defense Department "acted swiftly to address a cartel drone incursion. The threat has been neutralized and there is no danger to commercial travel in the region."

He said normal flights are resuming Wednesday morning.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/6554ae41-f93f-4e4e-a079-2302b81577bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)
* * *
* **STATE GOVERNMENT**

**" Attorney General Paxton, DOJ Announce $68 Million Settlement with Colony Ridge Developers"** [The Texan's](https://substack.com/redirect/e7749bfb-c7b2-447c-80eb-1a725736cbed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Meridith Dyer** - Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** , working with President **Donald Trump** 's Department of Justice (DOJ), announced a $68 million settlement against the developers of Colony Ridge.

The settlement addresses a 2023 federal lawsuit brought by the DOJ and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and a 2024 lawsuit filed by the Texas Office of the Attorney General in federal court, both alleging deceptive lending and marketing practices.

**" Transportation leaders support 'Hail Mary' plan to save DART, signaling election recalls"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/aac9dcd2-6ecf-403c-971d-38ef2ed8aa0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - The Regional Transportation Council voted Thursday to commit funds to DART's plan to give some resources back to cities, a proposal some suburban leaders said could persuade them to cancel May elections on cutting ties with the public transportation agency.

The 45-member transportation policy body of the North Central Texas Council of Governments approved committing $180 million to Dallas Area Rapid Transit, the Denton County Transportation Authority and the Trinity Railway Express. Of the commitment to regional transit, $75 million would go to DART's funding plan.

**Randall Bryant** , DART Board Chair, presented the plan to the agency's board of directors Tuesday, a proposal to save the regional transit system as Plano, Irving, Farmers Branch, Addison, University Park and Highland Park -- six of DART's 13 member cities -- near a deadline to call off withdrawal elections.

**" Fort Worth City Council hits 'pause' on $10 billion data center project"** [Fort Worth Star-Telegram's](https://substack.com/redirect/a5341537-5da8-4a3a-859c-d4f910274a61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **None** - The developer of a planned $10 billion data center in southeast Fort Worth has hit a speed bump in the rezoning of land for what could become one of the largest data center campuses in the metroplex.

Black Mountain, a Fort Worth-based energy consortium, has successfully petitioned the city to rezone roughly 431 acres of land in the southeast corner of the city near Forest Hill and Everman.

At the Fort Worth City Council meeting Feb. 10, Black Mountain was scheduled to ask the city to rezone another roughly 80 acres of land in two separate requests.

One of those requests is for about 42 acres on the east side of Anglin Drive near the Forest Hill city line. That request was rescheduled after leaders in nearby cities asked for a discussion with council member **Chris Nettles** , who represents that part of Fort Worth. The other request, for about 38 acres east of Anglin Drive and north of Everman Kennedale Road, was previously approved by the Zoning Commission.

**" Democrats Running for Texas Attorney General Vow to Reform Office Post-Paxton"** [The Texan's](https://substack.com/redirect/6bcbe27a-a192-4e39-adc8-5ecfddaaff91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Holly Hansen** - The open seat for Texas attorney general has drawn three candidates who are staking out positions in the runup to the March 2026 Democratic primary election by taking aim at the outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton, his potential Republican replacements, and, at times, each other.

Democratic candidates running for attorney general this year are state Sen. **Nathan Johnson** (D-Dallas), former Galveston Mayor **Joe Jaworski** , and former Federal Bureau of Investigation agent **Tony Box**.

**" Bexar County judge contenders rewrite history, talk over each other at fiery debate"** [San Antonio Report's](https://substack.com/redirect/5f215228-58a1-46a8-8826-02ea51ff840c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Andrea Drusch** - In a fiery one-hour debate Tuesday night, Bexar County Judge **Peter Sakai** and Democratic primary challenger **Ron Nirenberg** talked over one another, rewrote history on a major downtown development project and cast blame over who was at fault for a faltering relationship between city and county officials.

The two men overlapped as top leaders of a blue city and county -- Nirenberg as San Antonio mayor and Sakai as Bexar County's top executive -- for two and a half years.

Now opponents in a heated Democratic primary, they've gone deep into the weeds on past policy fights to differentiate themselves in a race where few ideological differences exist.

Early voting for the March 3 primary starts on Feb. 17.

**" Roy's SAVE Act Requiring Proof of Citizenship for Federal Voter Eligibility Passes U.S. House"** [The Texan's](https://substack.com/redirect/835a5d30-3726-4d68-9054-a0241671672b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Mary Elise O 'Bar** - Congressman **Chip Roy** 's (R-TX-21) legislation requiring proof of American citizenship to vote in federal elections passed the U.S. House on Wednesday, after similar versions passed the lower chamber twice in recent years before ultimately failing in the U.S. Senate.

Known as the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) or SAVE America Act, the bill would amend the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) of 1993 by requiring states to verify U.S. citizenship and identity through documentary proof in person when an individual registers to vote in federal elections, regardless of the registration method.

TOP NEWS " Southwest Airlines works to address issues with new assigned seating as customers fume" via - It's safe to say that Southwest Airlines ' transition to assigned seating is off to a turbulent start. Customers have taken to social media platforms for days to complain about things like lack of overhead bin space and not being allowed to switch seats, even when there are plenty open. Southwest, Love Field Airport's dominant carrier, began assigned seating on Jan. 27, ending its popular open seating policy. CEO Bob Jordan previously said that surveys conducted by Southwest showed customers and potential customers overwhelmingly wanted the option to pick their seat, similar to other major U.S. Airlines like Fort Worth-based American. The monumental switch was first announced in 2024. Around the same time, Southwest's management came under pressure following an activist takeover by Elliott Investment Management. () " American Airlines flight attendants vote no confidence in Isom as carrier underperforms" via - American Airlines' flight attendants have voted no confidence in the leadership of Robert Isom , the first time they have taken such an action against a sitting chief executive in its nearly 50-year history. The vote was unanimous amongst the board of directors for the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, the union that represents American's more than 28,000 flight attendants. It comes less than two weeks after the union called for new leadership. "From abysmal profits earned to operational failures that have front-line workers sleeping on floors, this airline must course-correct before it falls even further behind," said a statement from Julie Hedrick , president of the APFA. "This level of failure begins at the very top," she added. () " El Paso airspace closure was tied to Mexican cartel drones, White House official says" via - The Federal Aviation Administration reopened the airspace around El Paso International Airport in Texas on Wednesday morning, just hours after it announced a 10-day closure that would have grounded all flights to and from the airport. The Federal Aviation Administration said in a social media post that it has lifted the temporary closure of the airspace over El Paso, saying there was no threat to commercial aviation and that all flights will resume. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X that the FAA and the Defense Department "acted swiftly to address a cartel drone incursion. The threat has been neutralized and there is no danger to commercial travel in the region." He said normal flights are resuming Wednesday morning. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Attorney General Paxton, DOJ Announce $68 Million Settlement with Colony Ridge Developers" Meridith Dyer - Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , working with President Donald Trump 's Department of Justice (DOJ), announced a $68 million settlement against the developers of Colony Ridge. The settlement addresses a 2023 federal lawsuit brought by the DOJ and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and a 2024 lawsuit filed by the Texas Office of the Attorney General in federal court, both alleging deceptive lending and marketing practices. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " 5 council members seek formal reprimand over mayor's 'unprofessional conduct'" Andrea Drusch - Five members of the City Council are requesting a meeting to reprimand Gina Ortiz Jones over "repeated instances of unprofessional conduct." The move comes after Jones allegedly yelled at Sukh Kaur (D1) in a private meeting space last week, drawing a formal complaint from Kaur, and an investigation into whether the mayor violated the council's code of conduct. City Attorney Andy Segovia determined that outside counsel should look into the Feb. 5 incident, according to city spokesman Brian Chasnoff , and the City Council will receive a report once the investigation is complete. The council created a code of conduct in 2024 to address issues like inappropriate relationships with staff members, as well as set formal standards for how council members interact with one another and members of the public. () " Harris County to Provide Taxpayer-Funded Legal Assistance for H-1B Visa Applicants for County Jobs" Holly Hansen - Although Texas Gov. Greg Abbott ordered state agencies and universities to pause their use of a federal program that brings foreign workers to the country for specialized work amid allegations of fraud and abuse, Harris County will continue to use the program and provide some legal assistance to applicants. At the end of January, the Harris County Commissioners Court approved a contract as part of a consent agenda with Quan Law Firm to assist county employees with H-1B visa and Permanent Resident Card, also known as "Green Card," applicants. () " Transportation leaders support 'Hail Mary' plan to save DART, signaling election recalls" via - The Regional Transportation Council voted Thursday to commit funds to DART's plan to give some resources back to cities, a proposal some suburban leaders said could persuade them to cancel May elections on cutting ties with the public transportation agency. The 45-member transportation policy body of the North Central Texas Council of Governments approved committing $180 million to Dallas Area Rapid Transit, the Denton County Transportation Authority and the Trinity Railway Express. Of the commitment to regional transit, $75 million would go to DART's funding plan. Randall Bryant , DART Board Chair, presented the plan to the agency's board of directors Tuesday, a proposal to save the regional transit system as Plano, Irving, Farmers Branch, Addison, University Park and Highland Park -- six of DART's 13 member cities -- near a deadline to call off withdrawal elections. () " Fort Worth City Council hits 'pause' on $10 billion data center project" None - The developer of a planned $10 billion data center in southeast Fort Worth has hit a speed bump in the rezoning of land for what could become one of the largest data center campuses in the metroplex. Black Mountain, a Fort Worth-based energy consortium, has successfully petitioned the city to rezone roughly 431 acres of land in the southeast corner of the city near Forest Hill and Everman. At the Fort Worth City Council meeting Feb. 10, Black Mountain was scheduled to ask the city to rezone another roughly 80 acres of land in two separate requests. One of those requests is for about 42 acres on the east side of Anglin Drive near the Forest Hill city line. That request was rescheduled after leaders in nearby cities asked for a discussion with council member Chris Nettles , who represents that part of Fort Worth. The other request, for about 38 acres east of Anglin Drive and north of Everman Kennedale Road, was previously approved by the Zoning Commission. () 2026 " New Texas Primary Poll Shows Roy, Middleton Leading in Attorney General Race" Mary Elise O 'Bar - A new survey shows Congressman Chip Roy (R-TX-21) pulling ahead in the Texas attorney general race, while Texas comptroller candidate Don Huffines and incumbent Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller are similarly taking the lead in their Republican primary races. The poll, conducted by the University of Houston (UH) Hobby School of Public Affairs, collected responses from 550 likely voters in Texas for both the Republican and the Democratic primary elections, respectively, between January 20 and January 31. Both populations have a margin of error of +/- 4.18%. () " Democrats Running for Texas Attorney General Vow to Reform Office Post-Paxton" Holly Hansen - The open seat for Texas attorney general has drawn three candidates who are staking out positions in the runup to the March 2026 Democratic primary election by taking aim at the outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton, his potential Republican replacements, and, at times, each other. Democratic candidates running for attorney general this year are state Sen. Nathan Johnson (D-Dallas), former Galveston Mayor Joe Jaworski , and former Federal Bureau of Investigation agent Tony Box. During a recent forum attended only by Jaworski and Johnson, the candidates sparred over experience and whether a Democratic attorney general should work with Republicans in the state. "When you look at my opponent's record in the Senate, he is very comfortable cutting deals with [Lt. Gov.] Dan Patrick to keep his cherished committee vice chairmanship," said Jaworski. "That might be fine for the Senate, ladies and gentlemen, but it's not what we need in our lead attorney." () " Bexar County judge contenders rewrite history, talk over each other at fiery debate" Andrea Drusch - In a fiery one-hour debate Tuesday night, Bexar County Judge Peter Sakai and Democratic primary challenger Ron Nirenberg talked over one another, rewrote history on a major downtown development project and cast blame over who was at fault for a faltering relationship between city and county officials. The two men overlapped as top leaders of a blue city and county -- Nirenberg as San Antonio mayor and Sakai as Bexar County's top executive -- for two and a half years. Now opponents in a heated Democratic primary, they've gone deep into the weeds on past policy fights to differentiate themselves in a race where few ideological differences exist. "We may go back and forth, there may be a lot of words said," Sakai warned the crowd of more than 500 people at Stable Hall in his opening remarks. "But I'm asking you to look at who I am." Early voting for the March 3 primary starts on Feb. 17. () TEXANS IN DC " Roy's SAVE Act Requiring Proof of Citizenship for Federal Voter Eligibility Passes U.S. House" Mary Elise O 'Bar - Congressman Chip Roy 's (R-TX-21) legislation requiring proof of American citizenship to vote in federal elections passed the U.S. House on Wednesday, after similar versions passed the lower chamber twice in recent years before ultimately failing in the U.S. Senate. Known as the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) or SAVE America Act, the bill would amend the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) of 1993 by requiring states to verify U.S. citizenship and identity through documentary proof in person when an individual registers to vote in federal elections, regardless of the registration method. I will advocate for real solutions. | | | Peter, When my great-grandparents reached their twilight years in the 1990s, their care was shared among a dozen or so of their children and grandchildren. A nursing home cost around $25,000 per year. They had savings and their adult children were in a position to help. That world does not exist anymore. Today, as Baby Boomers enter their 70s and 80s, families are smaller. Fewer adult children are financially secure enough to step in. Nursing homes now cost more than $100,000 per year and the median American worker has just $955 in savings. **[If we don't move decisively as a country to provide robust safety nets and care for our people, ensure the prosperity of our workforce and the security of our seniors, we are going to begin an accelerated collapse that will echo into our children's generation.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvbKBRjijH4M6kFuhYdbd5oBt82e7oONi6Skce6kKgKdq8nvEi1ScTQklCY1mHCf8bYByWMgYvwSKT_FAlSXjqmzcDFUV_2MPZxzSM8NFrSheOFkYEQnxWATDmZK2RyTucT6aVH71utiqHMvrG_5EM4rJ-B5SPmPI7LcjhmqoUPjkp2yexgMDuOyTJnYRN2sA80L-Eyk7hXo3vbM2yRS7tQnxm9-qGerueLC-julkGSE0mVgNpsOrBeXrAOTRLOchwjzwBl2GVFZySqAvojnbBBo2eRLWk4EEq1VOJAaClU4BbMJ8AkDQuDe_C822Qqd10/4o8/h8sl6GIFQmeCE4liHqcgog/h0/h001.FZiEXwcxTqi1zE4jQ82gbf07Fh7YfThLr_nOldb7TOc)** I don't want my parents to live in fear of aging. I don't want my children to be crushed by cascading costs or a red ledger inherited from their parents and grandparents. For decades, politicians funded by billionaires and corporate PACs have cut taxes at the top while wealth and income concentrate further and further upward, and shrink the tax base that sustains Social Security and Medicare. Then those same politicians point to “shortfalls” and talk about cutting benefits. **[We will not dig ourselves out of this mess by electing the same bought-off politicians. That is why I have pledged to never accept money from corporate PACs.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvbKBRjijH4M6kFuhYdbd5oBt82e7oONi6Skce6kKgKdq8nvEi1ScTQklCY1mHCf8boENhlAGzpolkcdCVIx7WPBCDtKUsi2JEB-r6f-LHwAulslLilM0NcF0RUIq4XF8vJ-9s9wWYcKByfSxou2Mm8oxdGxGQJ16kdjV_FSUNgNZm0pO0hcR_pbNDTN_Y3qLyyhVZm1hcHaaSKO_PlKo4y3bAXZo0fpdDhtSJJjsgKyCGbGTF-GJFIKr7nBQHrLHUpnX8vYQkbo0rCRVkARpmJayTRLmUg0uQcJad8qcQRpUGYE2_SsFNX0xJ0lMEghgo/4o8/h8sl6GIFQmeCE4liHqcgog/h1/h001.giDvTpwaH9956ay1X9C2VEsOIjzdyusK7rie0UkPyEw)** I will advocate for real solutions. Medicare-for-All must cover senior and end-of-life care. We need to erase medical and student loan debt, mandate living wages, empower homeownership, uncap the Social Security tax, and tax extreme wealth to guarantee a dignified, basic existence. Will you help us build our campaign the right way, powered by working people and not a dime of corporate PAC money? “We may go back and forth, there may be a lot of words said,” Sakai warned the crowd of more than 500 people at Stable Hall in his opening remarks. “But I’m asking you to look at who I am.”

Early voting for the March 3 primary starts on Feb. 17.

Customers have taken to social media platforms for days to complain about things like lack of overhead bin space and not being allowed to switch seats, even when there are plenty open. » » Southwest, Love Field Airport’s dominant carrier, began assigned seating on Jan. 27, ending its popular open seating policy. CEO Bob Jordan previously said that surveys conducted by Southwest showed customers and potential customers overwhelmingly wanted the option to pick their seat, similar to other major U.S. Airlines like Fort Worth-based American. The monumental switch was first announced in 2024. Around the same time, Southwest’s management came under pressure following an activist takeover by Elliott Investment Management. (=) “American Airlines flight attendants vote no confidence in Isom as carrier underperforms” via = – American Airlines’ flight attendants have voted no confidence in the leadership of Robert Isom, the first time they have taken such an action against a sitting chief executive in its nearly 50-year history. The vote was unanimous amongst the board of directors for the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, the union that represents American’s more than 28,000 flight attendants. It comes less than two weeks after the union called for new leadership. “From abysmal profits earned to operational failures that have front-line workers sleeping on floors, this airline must course-correct before it falls even further behind,” said a statement from Julie Hedrick, president of the APFA. “This level of failure begins at the very top,” she added. (=) “El Paso airspace closure was tied to Mexican cartel drones, White House official says” via = – The Federal Aviation Administration reopened the airspace around El Paso International Airport in Texas on Wednesday morning, just hours after it announced a 10-day closure that would have grounded all flights to and from the airport. The Federal Aviation Administration said in a social media post that it has lifted the temporary closure of the airspace over El Paso, saying there was no threat to commercial aviation and that all flights will resume. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X that the FAA and the Defense Department “acted swiftly to address a cartel drone incursion. The threat has been neutralized and there is no danger to commercial travel in the region.” He said normal flights are resuming Wednesday morning. The settlement addresses a 2023 federal lawsuit brought by the DOJ and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and a 2024 lawsuit filed by the Texas Office of the Attorney General in federal court, both alleging deceptive lending and marketing practices. City Attorney Andy Segovia determined that outside counsel should look into the Feb. 5 incident, according to city spokesman Brian Chasnoff, and the City Council will receive a report once the investigation is complete. The council created a code of conduct in 2024 to address issues like inappropriate relationships with staff members, as well as set formal standards for how council members interact with one another and members of the public. At the end of January, the Harris County Commissioners Court approved a contract as part of a consent agenda with Quan Law Firm to assist county employees with H-1B visa and Permanent Resident Card, also known as “Green Card,” applicants. (=) “Transportation leaders support ‘Hail Mary’ plan to save DART, signaling election recalls” via = – The Regional Transportation Council voted Thursday to commit funds to DART’s plan to give some resources back to cities, a proposal some suburban leaders said could persuade them to cancel May elections on cutting ties with the public transportation agency. The 45-member transportation policy body of the North Central Texas Council of Governments approved committing $180 million to Dallas Area Rapid Transit, the Denton County Transportation Authority and the Trinity Railway Express. Of the commitment to regional transit, $75 million would go to DART’s funding plan. Randall Bryant, DART Board Chair, presented the plan to the agency’s board of directors Tuesday, a proposal to save the regional transit system as Plano, Irving, Farmers Branch, Addison, University Park and Highland Park — six of DART’s 13 member cities — near a deadline to call off withdrawal elections. Black Mountain, a Fort Worth-based energy consortium, has successfully petitioned the city to rezone roughly 431 acres of land in the southeast corner of the city near Forest Hill and Everman. At the Fort Worth City Council meeting Feb. 10, Black Mountain was scheduled to ask the city to rezone another roughly 80 acres of land in two separate requests. One of those requests is for about 42 acres on the east side of Anglin Drive near the Forest Hill city line. That request was rescheduled after leaders in nearby cities asked for a discussion with council member Chris Nettles, who represents that part of Fort Worth. The other request, for about 38 acres east of Anglin Drive and north of Everman Kennedale Road, was previously approved by the Zoning Commission. Democratic candidates running for attorney general this year are state Sen. Nathan Johnson (D-Dallas), former Galveston Mayor Joe Jaworski, and former Federal Bureau of Investigation agent Tony Box. During a recent forum attended only by Jaworski and Johnson, the candidates sparred over experience and whether a Democratic attorney general should work with Republicans in the state. “When you look at my opponent’s record in the Senate, he is very comfortable cutting deals with [Lt. The two men overlapped as top leaders of a blue city and county — Nirenberg as San Antonio mayor and Sakai as Bexar County’s top executive — for two and a half years. Now opponents in a heated Democratic primary, they’ve gone deep into the weeds on past policy fights to differentiate themselves in a race where few ideological differences exist. “We may go back and forth, there may be a lot of words said,” Sakai warned the crowd of more than 500 people at Stable Hall in his opening remarks. “But I’m asking you to look at who I am.” Early voting for the March 3 primary starts on Feb. 17. body:
For too long, we’ve settled for "safe" representation while the status quo remains untouched.

| | | | | [|
---](https://roseforcongress.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=35bf91c695e8f4a5dc8a9dd42&id=e2b50b3a05&e=8c53948e4c)

# #PickRose
---
| | After Prop 50, California’s 2nd District remains a stronghold of progressive values. In 2027, we know a Democrat will represent us in Washington. **The real question is: What type of Democrat will it be?**
For too long, we’ve settled for "safe" representation while the status quo of militarism and corporatism remains untouched. We are told we have to accept incremental change while our tax dollars continue to fund endless wars and human rights abuses abroad and healthcare costs skyrocket and home ownership dwindles.
With the challenges we face, "safe" isn't enough. We deserve a representative who refuses to be complicit in the face of global injustice and who fights for an agenda that centers "People, Peace, and Planet" right here at home.
[**But we need your help to make this bold vision a reality. Can you chip in now to bring our message to more voters in the district?**](https://roseforcongress.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=35bf91c695e8f4a5dc8a9dd42&id=ab71203348&e=8c53948e4c)
---

A victory for a Democrat is certain. A victory for a truly progressive, anti-war, pro-worker future is up to all of us.
**That’s why we say #PickRose.**
We are building this movement together, one conversation at a time. Rose would love to hear what's on your mind and share more about the campaign’s vision for CA-02.
Join us for Tuesday Tea with Rose Penelope Yee!
**When** : This Tuesday at 5:00 PM PST**Where:**[**RSVP for the Zoom here**](https://roseforcongress.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=35bf91c695e8f4a5dc8a9dd42&id=b43f7469f8&e=8c53948e4c)
Let’s talk about how we reclaim our government from the billionaires and war profiteers.
In solidarity,Team Rose

| | | | | | Hi –
**Early voting starts TOMORROW Tuesday, February 17th!!!**
This President’s Day, I wrapped up another full day of knocking doors and meeting the incredible people in our district – from a biologist, teacher, and artist to a finance guy, physicist, and retired professor!
I also met three former Republicans who are sickened by the current administration and plan to vote Democratic! 🤠
I was happy to chat with them about the state of our country and my vision for how we return it to normalcy, which is simple: elect good and smart people who love our country and understand the value of public service!
The San Antonio Express-News knows I am that servant leader, which is why they just endorsed me for a second time!
---
[|

subject: 18 Million Americans Are Using Marijuana Daily - NY Times Finally Admits It's Bad
body:
Plus: The most dangerous bill in NM just died — then the threats started | New for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=596497ae67&e=567664f14c)
| | | | | |
18 million Americans are now using marijuana daily. More than alcohol.
And the same newspaper that spent a decade pushing legalization just published what might be the most devastating reversal we've ever seen. [The numbers they buried are finally out](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=02b6f17060&e=567664f14c) — and when you see what this is doing to young men's brains, you'll understand why one expert says it's already too late.
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=1669a1dafd&e=567664f14c)
| |
🔥 **18 MILLION DAILY USERS — THE NEW YORK TIMES FINALLY ADMITS IT**
Daily use went from under 1 million in 1992 to 18 million today. That's not the scary number.
The scary number is what happens to young males within three years of heavy use. A doctor put out one stat that stopped us cold.
And the expert who spent years screaming about this? He was just asked, "What do we do now?" His answer is chilling.

🏛️ **NO REPUBLICAN ON THE BALLOT FOR U.S. SENATE — HERE'S THE REAL REASON**
For the first time in modern state history, there won't be a GOP candidate for Senate in New Mexico.
Turning Point's Tyler Bowyer blamed the state party. Mark explains why that comment reveals just how little he understands.
The inside baseball on why good candidates walked away — and why this is actually not the disaster people think it is.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=3f1205f1e8&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
🚨 **CLEAR HORIZONS CRUSHED 23-19 — THEN THE THREATS STARTED**
The most dangerous bill in the legislature just went down in flames. Seven Democrats crossed over to kill it.
Mark breaks down exactly how Mimi Stewart wired the bill to bypass the one committee that would've stopped it — and what we're hearing about what happened after the vote.
If ethics violations come out of this, you'll hear about it here first.

🇺🇸 **RUBIO JUST DELIVERED THE SPEECH OF THE YEAR — AOC GOT PANTSED ON TAIWAN**
Marco Rubio's Munich speech is the best Mark's heard in at least a year. We play it.
Then we play AOC being asked one straightforward question about defending Taiwan. Her answer is... something.

It's House Majority Leader Steve Scalise. I'm sending this message directly to your inbox because you are one of our top Patriots in your state.

ORIGINAL MESSAGEPATRIOT VOTER VERIFICATION SURVEY
You have been selected to participate in this important nationwide PATRIOT VOTER VERIFICATION survey project.
I offered to conduct this project as part of our Republican Party's mission to ensure that every single patriotic American citizen is registered to vote and fully empowered to guide our nation's future.
Your record stands out as a proud American, law-abiding taxpayer, and a registered voter living in: your state.
Please ensure our records are as accurate as possible by completing the VERIFICATION SURVEY below.
You are identified as a loyal patriot, so I am really counting on your prompt response. This project's results will be incomplete if we don't hear from you. And frankly, with everything at stake, your voice is urgently needed in our country's system of self-government.
As House Majority Leader, I am proud of everything I am doing to help President Trump enact his America First agenda. And I will not stop. Not ever. But the Democrats are spreading lies about the policies and getting their base of supporters riled up.
We've already seen left-wing "resistance" activists in communities across the country (including near your part of your state). And we are seeing Democrat Party committees and liberal PACs smashing fundraising records. All due to anti-Trump hatred.
If loyal patriots can't organize and mobilize on our own, the Woke Democrats will take back power and shut down our MAGA agenda. And they will spend President Trump's final two years in office attacking him with more Witch Hunts and impeachment drives.
That is why your immediate response is so important, Friend. I was honored to be selected by my colleagues to serve as Majority Leader. But I do not lead "from the top down." I listen to the grassroots . . . to patriotic men and women like you who love our country, share my conservative values, and want the best for our kids and grandkids. And I am confident that the best way to strengthen our movement - and score big victories at the polls in the Midterms- is by continuing to work shoulder to shoulder with you and other caring citizens.
To defeat the Woke Left and pass the rest of President Trump's MAGA agenda, we'll need REAL Americans to vote in large numbers. And we'll need them to cast informed votes.
That means pushing back against left-wing propaganda at every turn through next November. So please complete your VERIFICATION SURVEY and submit it TODAY.
And when you respond, I urge you to include one important gift of $250, $100, $50, $35, or any amount you can spare to my campaign. As I push the Trump Agenda through the House, forcing tough, narrow votes and speaking up for facts and the truth, I am coming under relentless attack from the left-wing campaign machine.
So please complete our voter verification survey as soon as possible. And don't forget to include your important gift of $250, $100, $50, or $35.
Every dollar will fuel my fight to pass more pro-America policies and mobilize a surge of MAGA voters to the polls this November. Thank you and God bless!
Steve ScaliseHouse Majority Leader

body:

|
Peter,
When I first ran for office in 2018, I was a young candidate running to be a Cook County Commissioner--trying to break into a political system that wasn't built for people like me.
I was offered a contribution of $56,500 from a corporate PAC.
For a first-time candidate running for a county-level seat, that is a staggering amount of money. That is the type of check that can swing an election. It's the kind of money that propels careers and secures victories.
But I didn't even have to think about it.
I refused the check.
---
| | [](https://e96gjzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0014NP-BgNPgyV6A9bG03ct_F75SKtULwg1lyOGqKsCFD1urp5TFbGQiKU4LnwJ6xyNB9sCfW6sIuS20oiljh0g5xup-B3PygtDhQsRdpR8fWdhI-aLzHeIfTpzuCIxUGb0KxQb-9gW8EiPKrHcYbE9fAxgyfKq0j2cmIGukfJIsubHjHwUA-ZtIfhTQrfCwm3IDM-kLZmp4QQchgp7g2oVJQs8GAjvhxrX&c=FcITx-Zypl_xluPLiXU7ua37t38NTFx3FsExvGtXWptzReBZCS4FIA==&ch=ZgZ9ABOlYhbzW23WYI5hXxFs9rbfX_7t_-bBkn39jmaO16RkO6vjZQ==)

## Amazon Cuts Ties with Surveillance Firm
Amazon's Ring [ended its partnership](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGupCAURL8Gdxi8qOiCxWzc9Wxnaa5yUaYRDNBter5-4kveF7xdJZVU5Zw_j_mBzruw_caDdLFxDnRlT6VQmpMLG5oF16fHvKe4UCrm9UY_g4CeC-CNmg06_5nbymhLBCQr0o1SjYRejrLaNQrbragGAUYMC9kehsE0IDuBNEoLldP3moBGNY3opaxHuXbdIkdQNI6t7FkryLgSU_03ulB2sv4T35TqNR6V13spZ2byF4OJwXRdV70u-aa4ewbTHRlMeOC_GLj1cX3yE1MJlPLuTk7BuLDx_DopLfHyHA3_ZmYwVUmb83Leu9wr1ortQOe_rsuPfL01_A8AAP__Q6SAbg) with law-enforcement technology company Flock Safety after its Super Bowl ad sparked privacy concerns. The ad showcased Ring's "Search Party" feature, which activates neighboring cameras to scan for a missing pet using AI. You can [see the ad here.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAUheGnwVssuNeGMjBUqrJUaaeq7YTA3ARaYiJMbKVPX6Wv0PUc6Rv-94M9uJTTfHpxZzLtWOxM25KpNaq2pvnkgnfTd3ZLrMVTbeG6umyBg9xx2Allg0v5ZocumCMREHZkhFICQaLGLhrBgyQ-SekG_jCgEAqdVzB6MQKMWnbJ3DUOQgnBJWKvcRpHjxoUaT2gZAOnkFqp_VdJc4t0zLeyUu2ncu6yia1dFoaPDPYM9tu29bdybVdP9_--uDZFhvuV4dNrpLef-rE818-umnDZUs5pkYoN_HR2Kf-R7V8dVgO_AQAA___5em_w) Critics said the technology could easily be turned on people, destroying privacy outside the home, and the Electronic Frontier Foundation labeled it a [surveillance nightmare](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupCAYRp8GOwwCwlBQbGM3225pEH5Hdn7FAGpmn37jTe4T3P7Ll3POn-f4dBHj9vrtVrB1TuMGV0GoFfKY4_ZyYXL-ja4sOU2QazhOhyNnXFHGaafH4CJ-RtkEOwNwEA3YTutOcCWMaBarpAbZeQFsEto8HrpnQUlmHr2BMAvfRHu_Md7prmNKiNYI3_eTMFyDMVIoIhmEWFNu_6a41QVm_KQTcuvT2qBdat0LEb8IHwgfrutqK_glw35MGP09InxwuUaPQPhw-1G3un9po7cgnTH5Ny1uhvqh5dgh0yldSMuRT4iIbvNAvyMQPjTZhv2KiLEoTSR7rS7iF0v9UcDT8v8BAAD__7_8hp4). Ring says the Flock deal, which would've let owners share their footage with law enforcement, [never went live](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ8Gd1hw8E9cUGzjLttuaR3gOGaDwQISK_v0K1_pPsFtphnp08z3577c0QcfH79xJ13XtEQ6S6BaKS_Zxwc6g_YZsGw5GcrVvd4YFhAwcAFcjotDHz5L1zi9EgGphrQcR6lgUJNqNg2qt5akFHBD098EWAlmklaJQRoxdY3XF02AHKUUg1LtpGzfGzXBSNPUqYF1gpyvKbd_k491ozV80ptya9PeBL3VehSmfjGYGcznebY2GnuVDOYLzWAWwGCWV-CO_1Is_PrGLUZLofA1JPvkB-YaKZfNHxx373h5HZS5SWfg6Pi3h3are2iydsfpQ_BlGFknHjv68DWo_sjiW8P_AAAA__8oMIVg), and no customer videos were ever shared.
## Olympic Medals: Payouts by Country
Olympic cash bonuses vary [wildly from country to country](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAUBOCnMZ0RPmbxUri4Dd3eNiXyz2FxYmxkHxbx9tFGeYO0M9Kn0Xw85ocJMaTnf7OhpiXPCc8akQjLXEJ6Gm-N-4qmriVbLOSPl4kzdDDwDrhQszchXnPfeL0gAsoGtVBKSBjkKJtVS-EHt8Ci7ovzON6Nt8L1CkbjoLcKm6DfWgdCCdENUrajdLeblSMoHMdeDqzv0AfKpf3MIdGKS7zyC0vr8tZEvRLtlcl_DCYG03merUvWvUsG05tmMHXAYBLDb8DPkAgLz_Ha9uAq39CbyG1OR-W7ufJBlduLu3wkKhc3tEYkrHwL0aTMXS4UkmlX2mJTtN_PEGOog2J999xMiD_L6E93vjR8BwAA__9yA4oY), with Singapore topping the list by doling out $792,000 for an individual gold medal, $395,000 for silver, and $197,000 for bronze, while countries like New Zealand, Canada, and Australia pay next to nothing [Team USA](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpSAQhZ8GO25gRkULim3o_m23NFwZlV0EA3iNb79xk32Cv_qmmHzn5Pz6mr6sDz6uP-1Oui5pinSVQLVSnrKPq3VvO_8Jtmw5vSlXd35smEBAzwVwqSZnfbintnF6IQLChrRUSiL0OGKzaVSydX1LywyDwKHtuoHGwfb4JuwGIRuvH5sAqaQUPeJrxLnr3jiConFssWetIOdryq_fyce60RLu9KH8mtPeBL3VehSGPxgYBua6rtdZbE3O3s8DA1NqyvfDI-VaGJgU7v3w83M-0QyMAAZGCgZmSxffz3njtm6BKhVONke-pMwvH6OP68NKmf-38J2cDfwsloEZVDeiQCmEYmCarN1x-RB86RVrxbpbH_7Vrt_a-qPhbwAAAP__gpuQyA) sits slightly below the middle of the pack, paying $37,500 for gold. That’s the 15th-highest among the 25 countries surveyed. Some countries take a different approach to sweeten the deal. In addition to cash, [Poland awards](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O5CAUhE-DMyx4YDwEDkajdTabbmi95qfN9rOxgGnLt191X2GTCiqo-vT9-V6-MVHa779xC1OLednDWSm0FspS0n5Hf0P3IKxrybdQmv95Ii0gwHABXI6Lx0TXojs_xRAgqC5MchylAqOs6tbJehdB3iSCBhMdOmH0h_XRoJXKRdml6bUmQI5SCqNUb5UbhpuyMAZrtTJMi-BTy6X_m9Pe1hDpys9Qepe3jqa1taMy9clgZjCf59kfmeojhYI-5f4gBrOyA4N5HK1gMGNp1-PnXRutB2MZfB2ZcPc8xxhK5Zmu7UiOuxW3I-W98tcfZzD8AgbDxys-v0ALIQRPO3dYVx4JW-UxF37P5PkWPFLtyuSPMxGlakamxX3DRG_w9l-2nxP8CwAA__98CJDV) its Olympians a two-room apartment, jewelry, and a Toyota Corolla for winning gold. Other countries, like Great Britain, Sweden, and Norway, [don’t pay](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQAF8DHcjeBSMXLtLQXdqUaLH3wImxke27E7-PLl9IP5qR5uu23MgHH7dPOtjUe1oiv0rgWjkv2ceN3Er2J1DZc1o5V_d4UlhAgOoEdHJaHPlwLUPrzJ0ZGFs2cpokgkKN7W6EHXgcVyWJUJFGrZySGgEGRIF2bb152wTISUqhEHuNdhxX1DCx1gOqZhDsfE25_04-1p3v4UpPzr1NRxvMXutZGvxoYG5gLmfKtfQX7Sm9gQZmytXbwKWB2aZHrNlz6U66uiOV2r18jD5u3cGOQumkHkYYhYJ-r0dos3Hny4fgi5qaQWwH-fDXrf-a9TTwGwAA__-wZn2K) their medalists at all.
## Oscar-winning Actor Robert Duvall Dies at 95
Robert Duvall, the Oscar-winning actor whose seven-decade career produced some of the most iconic [performances in American cinema](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOpDAQBNCvgczItI05Bw4uIZtLL0QNboPvjD0yvcPO369m9hM2LqlKr_7e5hvGFPP2Bw9yHMqc6ToTMVOda8wb-gXX_wnPvZaFKvuPB6YZJBghQfTj7DGm56xb7wIRkGrJ9ePYKzDKqnZ3ZILURL8WBIJBaQq4DANaVFoZWm0b3atNQj_2vTRKdVatw7AoCyNZq5VptCQfudTuX4mZdwrpWR5Uu7UcbXI78_1s1O8Gpgam67q6UD5filfewESZqTLGfFDmBqat-IC8UxUnYxXfLPF2JeEJvbBDW52_XzGleJqx0XI7MKb3Hv_opIeDrwAAAP__bNR89w), died Sunday at his Virginia home. He was 95. Duvall earned seven Academy Award nominations and won Best Actor for 1983's _Tender Mercies_. He’s best remembered as Gus McCrae in _Lonesome Dove_ , the stoic Corleone consigliere Tom Hagen in _The Godfather_ , the surf-obsessed Lt. Col. Kilgore in _Apocalypse Now_ , and the fiery preacher in _The Apostle_ _,_ a passion project he [wrote, directed, and financed himself](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkEGOtCAUhE-jOww8RH8WLP6Nu57tLM0DnsoMDQbpNn37iT1HmF1VKqnUV5-3-YYhhrR-4J1MXfKc6Dwi1UplLiGt6C2674jHVrKlUv3jiXEGDgPjwMQ4ewzxNfetNwsRkGzJiHEUEgapZbsZMcCgpBVc9Va5BZ3yhAtYzZ0S0ts2mKuNgxiF4IOUnZZOKSs1jKR1L4em5-RDzaX7yiHVjZb4yk8qncv3Npqt1v1o5P8Gpgam8zy7ZN1FceUNTJdsYMo21AeWQJf5ZWFvmMjQ1VzYmv2CdaPCcM8O42s_iKV8Mh_oYFqx4hL20Mt_bTF-P0OM4RjGpufrHUN8r6l_uvBp4CcAAP__ExqG0w). His wife, Luciana, said he passed peacefully at home. The family asked fans to honor his memory by watching a great film or telling a good story with friends. [See his life in photos](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMR3IXoMdChfX0OXaK5HB6-C7BUf2XhBv_yv5H-GvRxrNN3_u890nSsfjt9_RcczzgWclZMYyl3Q8fFj8-o983UpesHD4__I0gwTTSmiVnYNPdM19E1xEBNQNOmWt0mD0qJvNBWOGIEeExY7xFgbpTb_eolWxj6vtfZPcu02CskpJo3U36nUYFj2CxXHstRG9xJA4l-5vTgdvGOnKLyzdmveG3Mb8rEL_EjAJmM7z7C6_5fxOBUx4MBb26djxYAHTioRLSXwJmHzhtBJWAdM3rv3oqLaUIrbPLXOurbppA3owptt4p6a48DwTUarGil4-dp_os4R_dN_LwVcAAAD__8MchOc).

## Cave Researcher Rescued
A team of more than 60 people from multiple agencies [rescued](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuqzAMhp8mbEGJgUCGDHdh613viNzElNymUDlpad_-iOpI5wHOZsn2r__7_p2mE8YU18tfvJErr3mbVtpzolKIp7j-fzAFj09iyoTsF2Km7CdQYKQCqfspYEzvqa2CO6tgdUVO971uwJpuqBaHg7HWBAxnq03XtWputG3VoIFahY2qojvCFOheg1Kdqc86hMHOOGjoBtuRaBWFWDauy0KFXpjn9N6exLXfblVySyn3LJo_AkYB477v9ZXK9VgKGA8aAePnTcD4TSR_cI7RPyjIuMqdcpGfU4lzIZZ5Y09MnOXhQPLmrzOmJGCs2IX7HlOK2fSiVZcbxvQpVH6n8engKwAA__9ya4ke) an injured researcher from Terrell County's Sorcerer's Cave on Sunday morning. The woman is currently being treated at a hospital in Odessa. A group of researchers was studying the Sirion River at the bottom of the 567-foot-deep cave, one of the [deepest](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLtu9CAQhZ8Gd6xgfMEuKP7G3f5tSmsM4zURNhbgvbx9xCZSHiDdSPPp6Jzv4zpd0Xm33_7jRjo_lzDt9EiecqY4uf3zjGQN3ilSIoxmpRgpmQkEdFwAl2qy6PxraiqrZ2EHWZGWSskahq7tq1XXCoyaB5hn7EXbEvWNbNQyo7UwdE1dOV3CBEglQYi2u8zS2n5YsJfQ9kNLrBFkXQ7xklfK9MS0-Fe4U7yYsFVerzkfidX_GIwMxnSQyfHcfDDoy5ZCMRjzszzDmVf-zuDk-YEpMBgLxWAsNRiMAhiMslzfHN5oN44SL8NP4rjzHy_8VwpfYth4EVVFbY-H896lTrFG3DZ0_t00_83vXcNXAAAA___VuJCj) in Texas. As they were ascending out of it on Saturday, one of them was hit by a falling rock at a depth of about 470 feet at around 6 p.m. The group didn't reach a point where they could [call for help](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGS4yAQRU-DMlTQAoECgk2UedMNVS1oLHaw5ELYsm8_JSdzgIl_16t-799lumDKab3-xRu5-orbtNKxZ6qVypTW_49CweOTCu2ExS9UCu1-AgE9F8ClmQKm_J5UE9wswiAbctIY2cHQa9sszgLY2FHnI4aOhk4aRTFGJYYwe5C6Se6ECZBGghC6b2cZgh0iWgnaDpqYEhRS3UpbF6r0wj3m9_ak0vrt1mS31HrfWfeHwchgPI6jPSLiOTIYsdTkMzEYTy8GY948ZgbjB8Rg_BHjp9mDAv9MPBDdaa_8a92OlZ8NznOwhlstyQBa3us4cyX9zGdFketBKxGU7q3GprhwP1LOae8NU-J6w5Q_D9ffZX46-A4AAP__NbiQkA) until 9 p.m. During the ensuing rescue operation, the injured researcher was assisted through narrow "squeezes"—including one measuring just 12 inches by 36 inches—and several vertical pits ranging from 30 to 90 feet deep. The team finally [exited the cave](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OwyAQhJ_G7rAA_1JQXJMu115pbbxLzAmbCDZx_PYn8gpXz2g-ffNzna_gg9_v37CR5beL805HDsRMafb77zMRLvCiRJkgLSulRHmZtdSDkFqocUbw4Zy7Gu1NolE1WTWOqtVm6Kd6tcoZwAWndnIGVDf0WraA3Q2pW5Tpofa2jEmtRqWl7IfmphAn42BSup9MT1UnCT3H1PBKTG_ILpzxRalZ4lYHuzI_ctV-VfpS6ctxHI2L7xGemf1eKpW-FKeSxQ12UQSehMKluIm4k0CiB2UWxVPkMzNt4sOpk8XH4UPweRirTt438OFD5f999bL6LwAA__-9HICu) around 4:45 a.m. Sunday morning. Agencies participating in the rescue effort include the U.S. Border Patrol's Search, Trauma, and Rescue team, Texas Game Wardens, Texas DPS, Terrell County Sheriff's Office, Sanderson and Fort Stockton Fire Departments, San Antonio Technical Rescue, and National Cave Rescue Commission.
## School Districts Reject Optional Prayer Period
A new state law requires every Texas school district to hold a vote on implementing an optional prayer and Bible reading period during the school day by March 1. With the deadline approaching, numerous districts have opted not to do so. | | Friends,
With county conventions approaching on February 26, the most important decision before us is nominating a Republican who can win in November. These conventions will select delegates to the March 28 State Endorsement Convention, and I want to briefly reintroduce myself and explain why I believe I am the best candidate to serve as Michigan's next Attorney General and defeat the Democrat nominee.

As you consider who to support at the State Endorsement Convention, I believe the choice is straightforward.
