I am also endorsed by organizations such as the Southeast Michigan Chamber of Commerce and the Police Officers Association of Michigan, along with a growing number of current and former legislators.
Those endorsements represent credibility. Credibility builds trust with voters, strengthens the Republican ticket, and wins statewide elections.
While I bring experience, results, and broad support, other candidates on both sides of the aisle carry serious personal and professional controversies. Voters are being asked to overlook scandals, ethics concerns, and troubling workplace records. Michigan deserves better, and I am confident voters will recognize the difference in November.
I appreciate your time and your involvement in this important process. You can learn more about me at votedouglloyd.com or find additional interviews and appearances at linktr.ee/douglloydforag.
I respectfully ask for your support at your county convention and at the State Endorsement Convention on March 28 at the Novi Vibe Showplace. Together, we can nominate a proven conservative leader who is ready to win and serve the people of Michigan.
Sincerely,
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. | For those of us who believe in democratic values and live in rural areas, the choices are rarely simple. We have fewer options, wider philosophical gaps, and we are often voting for a first time candidate. Too often, the underdog.
Even for deep blue, capital D Democrats, the decision is not always straightforward. Voting in rural districts means balancing principle and strategy. But the beauty of voting is this: it is yours alone, and the only wasted vote is the one not cast.
That brings me to Congressional District 3 and [Marie Gluesenkamp Perez](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwRM0WRcqi70vJIaM0C-mVhDVOfdDRFduZXa1h4692U5Ju4oR3waXv8QpR3sMeBHviDlglOsseAapOyHVmF5sFs6PL4UAsokw3p-9S15Ws-y_0=&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==), a [Blue Dog Democrat](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwRSiqMAq9X4HifY7OlFNsPv9vLnK-wHu_9gawAWjMYN5z-UOHcjhr9T2REVf-bR80EuRhctqHEd2xypm1LII0g-A==&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==). She has been under scrutiny for her voting record. She reportedly votes with Republicans about 48 percent of the time, which unsettles many left leaning constituents.
The flashpoint has been her support for funding ICE. Her explanation was that fully funding ICE allows oversight and control. Reading it, I could not help but picture a tantrum throwing child being appeased in hopes of maintaining order. Who is controlling whom? Still, someone I respect reminded me that she has held this seat for two cycles. That matters. Incumbency carries weight. She knows her district.
---
| | [](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTixf3wRUp5ZcYbq4tocpYH1Apt_RBWHI_xO5hYr2iv6RtVuHBZpvCskWxAs-APhMDZjjhrredXO0Hq5eQ4W3_GMQeyjLYAnNd86OmpI2AZCZS-jPrVF34dA=&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==)

| Facebook post February 3, 2026
But there are others in the race. [Brent Hennrich](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwRIJAP8jkkpo7yApUvUgYgc8YrYbxwnYqEJ4KKapq0ZW6S3_njE5crMs1a4PWY9ZTaqCNI63ff_xZOyTOtBa0VHow-YWckRHzL&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==) ran in 2022 and stepped aside to consolidate votes behind her. He is now back. After her January 22 vote on ICE funding, his campaign raised 50,000 dollars in small dollar donations in ten days. Polling commissioned by his campaign suggests that only about 24 percent of her previous voters feel confident supporting her again. Many supported her more as a vote against Joe Kent than as an endorsement of her.
So what does a Democrat do? Support the incumbent because she may have the strongest path to reelection? Support a challenger whose platform aligns more closely with traditional Democratic views? Or stay home and risk handing the seat to the favored Republican, [John Braun](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwR2bhKbJbiE7ZI-3KBY8N2QH7RuxvwyL1mpHBvTP19iu1lUTueJcV0RQZdviNDyfKIX7xB2s6FWhtM0d-0iBtF3vS0i2afJkvAL98KOviK5EA=&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==)?
In Congressional District 4, I have heard Democrats say they voted for Dan Newhouse to reward his impeachment vote. Others did so out of fear that Jerrod Sessler would win. Rural Democrats make complicated choices.
But one truth remains. If Democrats show up and vote, we win. Especially in midterms, when turnout is low and margins are thin.
So vote.

| Using early research into voting patterns, Washington State seems on-track for turnout of about 65% in the upcoming Midterm. Throughout Washington, expected turnout varies across counties. Rural and Eastern counties make up some of the highest-turnout (San Juan, Garfield, Wahkiakum) and lowest-turnout (Adams, Grant, Franklin). These results follow demographics (age, ethnicity, and education level) but also reflect longstanding local nuances. When it comes to turnout, politics are often local.

I recently had an enlightening conversation with Danielle Surkatty of the [Yakima Immigration Response Network](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwRMYdoYi1_3e3U-c6TB5UnSMR5U4D2zPkFtBXu2Kmqf0oZ02sVkfAOBXyFa3mdkLsdfGH0fX68ZzAYwGe7I17hg8GPKWkYYUCWAFQ6FGwizTJClk5Kg-63MypI7Hh4MV5H&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==), YIRN. She founded the organization in 2017, and it has grown into one of the most trusted community support networks in Central Washington.
Since the start of the Trump administration, the need for YIRN's services has grown dramatically. Yakima County now has the highest number of ICE arrests in Washington State, according to the [University of Washington Center for Human Rights.](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwRiqINOcpwezmpaI1WGFKBP-2pb-V_H6pcY4VEnzi6CS0fFzDeCAxcCF6HGEbbj0aSqOu-jevbXV1nNIfVgln8O9lEafOgTY02QBnNd6U7aBhMSxmTgH579Q==&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==)
An ICE arrest is not just a statistic. It is a family crisis. Imagine living paycheck to paycheck and a spouse suddenly disappears. No clear answers. No immediate information. Just fear, uncertainty, and children who still need to be fed and protected. YIRN steps into that chaos. They accompany people to court dates. They place funds into commissary accounts. They provide gas cards and emergency support. They help secure passports for U.S. born children. They counter misinformation and ensure families understand their rights. Volunteer and ICE victim Jamie Ortiz has started a [Facebook page](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwRl-TEiKZr8SJ2d_JAwL2Y4837gBfNPzpgIMauJIhUGJN79MGZKK2Q9sJkYMm8HvIW1YlFpzEGot7JMEOGJBa-CiYr3HtdbEnegvtT6J6aghFYLX6vFnUyuQ==&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==) to monitor ICE activity. It now has over twenty eight thousand followers.

| Washington's [Keep Washington Working Act](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018IMa7WkBslfMJtDFdRDLDEYFA-NkdbplmdNVlTiey7b8YSPn--WeTn2b_p-bmNwRGxgd0fV4pftQyRPP0G47rk994yDe71MKv5aKNITpRezW9iJ_APCpNUiFR1JzlRRA-cs4aWhZXvgQDushOPOkEpy9lrbbfuPKtYpLw_BIuIRHkF1qtkgqE1_4a9hC_c1KrZeN3-VS4v2RLLkjBdmNMw==&c=0T_wGwTereP73pO-h6nxRH1zJSZNBVIxAlronWZUaQijyaCSsI8ibA==&ch=kYUuCVD9fRzZw_QdOJwR-LamPKzZGwcUETCVucm7AbJl-ru8O_mMYw==) restricts state and local law enforcement from assisting ICE, and Yakima County Sheriff Bob Udell has stated his office will not assist ICE operations. Still, families remain vulnerable, and the need is real.
YIRN has built a strong coalition to support impacted families, and they rely on volunteers and direct financial contributions to sustain this work.

It's not the first time, and I've even had the _police_ called on me for trespassing. **All for simply trying to conduct oversight — as is my right as a Member of Congress.** Look, I'm an immigrant. My children are first-generation Americans. Every day, I read stories and watch videos of innocent people being violently detained and uprooted from their lives to serve Trump’s _sick_ political agenda. **As a human being,** I’m completely repulsed by what's going on in our country. **As a father,** I’m deeply worried for all the immigrant kids who are scared right now. **As a Congressman,** I’m livid that Kristi Noem and Donald Trump are carrying out these attacks on innocent people – and trying to hide it from ANY oversight. **It’s my JOB to do this. As a member of the House Committee on Oversight, it’s my responsibility and legal right to hold these people to account.** But the MAGA loyalists in the White House and Senate have made clear they have zero respect for the law – or the basic rights of our neighbors. This fight is personal to me. Trump’s policies are breaking apart families and putting lives in danger. So yes – _I’m angry._ **But look, Peter – if I've learned anything in my life as an immigrant in this country, it’s that success comes from translating our anger and worry into _action_.** That’s why I’m running for Senate. Because we need leaders with a backbone to FIGHT BACK against these attacks and stop Donald Trump before it’s too late. ---
| | Friend,
---
| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn’t a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal — the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God’s grace.**

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**“God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold.”**_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.
---
[](https://trk.mg.swampdigest.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=talwz0&__onlt=h)
---
When you read it, you will hear Charlie’s voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie’s hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

**[To claim your copy of this life-changing book, simply make a generous gift in any amount to Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.mg.swampdigest.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=talwz0&__onlt=h)**

---
In the months since Charlie’s assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA’s message among young Americans...

...and it’s not just the conservative message as a whole — _**it’s the message of FAITH!**_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie’s call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it’s happening._

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we’re witnessing is not just growth —**it’s revival.**

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America’s faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up.**

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _“We’re not backing down.”_

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie’s most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie’s faith._**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

**[To claim your copy of Charlie’s final book, simply make a gift, in any amount, to support Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.mg.swampdigest.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=talwz0&__onlt=h)**

---
I’ll personally ensure your copy is sent to you as soon as possible.

Thank you in advance for carrying on Charlie’s mission and supporting his legacy.
---
**For Charlie,**

**Justin Streiff**
Chief Operating Officer
Turning Point USA

| | | (_[Go straight to action](https://default.salsalabs.org/T22ab5313-13f5-4cfa-9270-d01a5ec155f9/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)_ | _[Other actions](https://default.salsalabs.org/Ta33f3597-173b-4f98-95af-26e649db6062/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)_ ) When Stephen Colbert interviewed Texas state Rep. (and US Senate candidate) James Talarico, he did what late-night satire has always done: challenge power, give voice to those fighting back, and wrap it all in a wonderfully delicious layer of humor. But [CBS ordered](https://default.salsalabs.org/T44da35c4-9809-4c0b-b1d7-94bc249f1f87/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) him to pull the segment. Why? Because it might run afoul of Trump's FCC, which has no problem censoring content, especially from Trump's political opponents. And with Talrico running for US Senate, and mounting a strong campaign, it was clear they didn't want him exposed to a national audience. **[So CBS caved](https://default.salsalabs.org/T17a1a097-3c8b-4063-94ef-219fd7aabf88/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9), and told Colbert he couldn't have Talrico on, and couldn't even talk about this (which he of course proceeded to do as soon as he started the show).** Let's be clear about what is happening here. Trump and his lackeys are using government power to silence the voices of both critics and political opponents. And CBS caved with barely a whimper. This does not end well. And we need to demand they halt right now. **[Add your name, and tell CBS and the FCC:"Don't Silence Stephen Colbert, and Hands off Our Freedom!"](https://default.salsalabs.org/T8f56ea41-7cff-49f4-a6e6-58ba65349226/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) **

Peter,
Let's be brutally honest about what we're dealing with.
While Trump posts AI-generated videos depicting the Obamas as apes, threatens to invade sovereign nations, covers up Epstein files with heavily redacted documents, prosecutes the Federal Reserve Chair, and sends ICE agents to "surround" polling places--
Some people are still treating this like politics as usual.
They're not.
Newsflash: This moment is anything but normal.
We're not dealing with a traditional Republican president who respects institutions and democratic norms.
And the playbook that worked against Mitt Romney or John McCain? It won't work here. You can't fact-check your way out of authoritarianism. You can't win a rigged game by following rules your opponent abandoned years ago.
You have to FIGHT BACK.
Here's the good news: Some Democrats GET IT.
Leader Jeffries understands the redistricting battle is existential - and he's helping lead the national fight. California passed Prop 50 and the Supreme Court let it stand. New York City eliminated the last GOP seat in the region. Virginia and Maryland are joining the counteroffensive.
These Democrats understand that abnormal threats require bold responses.
But it's not enough for leadership to get it. Grassroots Democrats need to step up and DEMAND that we match Trump's assault on democracy with an equally aggressive defense.
That's what Colorado Draws the Line is all about.
We're not waiting for permission. We're not debating whether fighting back is "too aggressive." We're putting a ballot initiative in front of Colorado voters that will flip 3-4 congressional seats and destroy MAGA's gerrymandering scheme.

In 2015, German Chancellor Angela Merkel uttered the infamous words "Wir schaffen das" ("We can do this"), unilaterally suspending the 2003 [Dublin Regulation](https://substack.com/redirect/d6b13935-6274-4da5-abc1-f21acc8f0ac9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and flinging open Europe's borders to over a million migrants, primarily from Syria, Afghanistan, and North Africa. This wasn't a humanitarian reflex but a calculated policy, as Merkel herself later admitted multiculturalism had "utterly failed" in Germany--yet she doubled down, inviting cultural chaos that would metastasize into the West's defining crisis of unchecked illegal immigration.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.n1PyoQGfeXcucQn2sJl8vmIzjI4vDDPYbgKY0qAi9GY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=188269951)
We now know from reports, primarily from Der Spiegel based on Snowden documents, that the NSA targeted Merkel's personal mobile phone as early as 2002 (during the Bush administration) and continued until at least 2013. The surveillance reportedly involved a listening unit in the U.S. Embassy in Berlin and included her phone number on an NSA target list.

Obama publicly acknowledged the revelations damaged U.S.-German relations and perceptions of U.S. intelligence. He implemented reforms, including curbs on spying on allied leaders' communications.
The incident strained U.S.-German ties, with Merkel famously stating "spying among friends is not acceptable."

Far from an isolated German blunder, Merkel's decision ignited a domino effect, normalizing mass migration as a tool of globalist agendas, eroding national sovereignty, and fueling populist backlashes from Brexit to Trump's border wall.

Merkel's gamble began with Syrian refugees fleeing civil war, but it quickly devolved into an uncontrolled influx of economic opportunists and potential security threats. By 2016, Germany alone absorbed 1.2 million arrivals, straining welfare systems, housing, and public services to breaking point. [Sexual assaults in Cologne on New Year's Eve 2015](https://substack.com/redirect/3223c0cd-b91f-4d32-a423-dc4cfbb28535?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--perpetrated overwhelmingly by migrants--exposed the naivety, or worse, the deliberate blindness, to integration failures. Migrants from incompatible cultural backgrounds rejected Western values, forming parallel societies in cities like Berlin's Neukolln, where no-go zones emerged amid rising crime rates: violent offenses surged 10% in 2016, with non-citizens overrepresented in statistics.

Merkel knew the risks; her East German Stasi-honed pragmatism ensured she foresaw the backlash. Yet, she branded critics "Nazis," stifling dissent and entrenching a pro-migration orthodoxy across Europe.

The ripple effects were seismic. Merkel's signal acted as a beacon, drawing millions more to the continent via the Mediterranean route--over 1.5 million crossings by 2017, per UNHCR data. Balkan smuggling networks exploded, turning the EU into a porous sieve. Southern nations like Greece and Italy buckled under the weight, while Northern states faced secondary migrations, with Sweden's rape crisis (up 1,472% since 1975, largely migrant-linked) and [France's banlieue riots](https://substack.com/redirect/d173db47-15d6-4341-bc47-cc65a6bde77b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) epitomizing the fracture. The EU's failed quota system only deepened divisions, as Hungary's Viktor Orban built fences Merkel decried as "un-European." By weaponizing guilt over Holocaust atonement, she globalized victimhood narratives, inspiring copycat policies from Canada's Trudeau to Biden's border reversals.

In the U.S., Merkel's shadow looms large. Her 2015 pivot echoed Obama's DACA expansions and sanctuary city proliferation, inviting Central American caravans that overwhelmed the southern border--over 10 million encounters since 2021. American "Merkels"--from Pelosi's open-tent rhetoric to Soros-funded NGOs ferrying migrants--mirror her blueprint: dismantle enforcement, reframe illegality as "humanity," and suppress data on costs (e.g., $150 billion annually in U.S. welfare for non-citizens). Deindustrialization followed suit; Merkel's nuclear shutdowns and green mandates gutted German manufacturing, paralleling U.S. offshoring that hollowed Rust Belt towns, now migrant influx flashpoints.

Merkel's defenders claim demographics demanded influxes for aging Europe, but this ignores her sabotage of family policies and the cultural erasure she enabled--Arabic over German in some schools, Sharia patrols in London. Her post-chancellorship silence as the AfD surges to 20% approval indicts her complicity. The West's immigration crisis--fractured communities, strained budgets, eroded trust--is her Frankenstein: a borderless utopia birthed in Berlin, now devouring democracies. Justice demands accountability; how many more "Merkels" must we unmask before reclaiming our civilizations?

Lately, I've been doing some reflecting on my grandfather, President John F. Kennedy, and his legacy of hope.
In my run to fight for NY-12 in Congress, and just as a person, that's what I want to focus on. Hope.
My name is Jack, or John Bouvier Kennedy Schlossberg if you want to know the whole thing.
In high school, I spent hours watching my grandfather's speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. When we fight for hope, we're not just doing it for ourselves, we're doing it for each other and the future we all have to share.
I know I have big shoes to fill. In my grandfather's memory, I've led a life of caring about this a lot. I put that care and effort and hope into everything I do.
But this is bigger than me. It's bigger than my family's legacy.
Hope is hard to find in Politics these days, but if we let it die out completely, that's how we really lose. Now cannot be the time to stop caring or turn away. We have to double down in our pursuit of hope.
I really think this election is the one — our last chance to stop Trump and change the direction we're heading in.

| | Friend,
---
| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn’t a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal — the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God’s grace.**

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**“God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold.”**_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.
---
[](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=talzzd&__onlt=h)
---
When you read it, you will hear Charlie’s voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie’s hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

**[To claim your copy of this life-changing book, simply make a generous gift in any amount to Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=talzzd&__onlt=h)**
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA**
**& Receive Charlie’s Final Book**](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=talzzd&__onlt=h)
---
In the months since Charlie’s assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA’s message among young Americans...

...and it’s not just the conservative message as a whole — _**it’s the message of FAITH!**_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie’s call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it’s happening._

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we’re witnessing is not just growth —**it’s revival.**

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America’s faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up.**

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _“We’re not backing down.”_

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie’s most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie’s faith._**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

**[To claim your copy of Charlie’s final book, simply make a gift, in any amount, to support Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=talzzd&__onlt=h)**

---
I’ll personally ensure your copy is sent to you as soon as possible.

Thank you in advance for carrying on Charlie’s mission and supporting his legacy.
---
**For Charlie,**

**Justin Streiff**
Chief Operating Officer
Turning Point USA

| | Peter ,

I'm proud to announce that **Combat Vets for Congress has officially endorsed my campaign** for Nevada's 4th District!
---
| [ ](https://electdavidflippo.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9aba26b775663b53df718fc1a&id=299f388a7d&e=273c9a71fb)

| This powerful organization of combat veterans recognizes me as the proven, battle-tested leader who will bring the same fighting spirit I showed in uniform to Congress. Just like when I was in the Air Force, I commit to **defending our country** , **supporting our brothers and sisters in arms** , and **putting America First** every single day.
As a retired U.S. Air Force Lieutenant Colonel with 24 years of service, I commanded over 1,000 Airmen in combat, established forward operating bases in Iraq during the height of the fight, earned the Bronze Star for valor, and dedicated my life to protecting our freedoms. Combat Vets for Congress sees that same dedication in my commitment to:
✅**Fully fund and modernize our military** so our troops have the best equipment and readiness. ✅**Expand healthcare** , **mental health support** , and **job opportunities for veterans** : because no one who served should ever be left behind. ✅**Keep our border secure** from any of the threats that endanger our communities and our veterans. ✅**Cut wasteful spending and balance the budget** so we can afford a strong defense without bankrupting future generations.
This endorsement means the world to me. It’s validation from fellow warriors who know what real service looks like. _**They trust me to carry that same resolve to Washington**_.
We need your help to turn this momentum into victory and replace the current representation with a Congressman who truly **understands sacrifice** and will always have our backs.
**I am matching every single dollar donated, so your donation will have 2X the impact!**
Your gift will power our fight to bring veteran leadership, strength, and America First priorities to Congress.

#

**Never forget what we’re up against.**
It wasn’t long ago when the NRA’s magazine featured a story with the words “Target Practice” next to a picture of Gabby and Nancy Pelosi.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/63703?c0=giffords-em-q12026.1ZloXK&refcode=em250217-1-b&t=1&akid=11262%2E3935704%2EDyzvma)
The NRA knows that guns are the number one killer of children and teens in America.
They know that a majority of Americans support commonsense gun safety measures like background checks and closing dangerous loopholes.
But they don’t care. Not when it affects their bottom line.
The gun lobby has spent decades pushing the narrative that owning a gun makes you safer and that being allowed to carry a gun around in public is an exercise of freedom. They don’t, and it’s not.
Freedom is being able to exist in public spaces without having to worry whether someone next to you has a gun.
The gun lobby will stoop to desperate lows to fearmonger their base, including sending messages like these.**That won’t stop GIFFORDS in our fight to save lives.**
At GIFFORDS, we will continue fighting to empower voters at the ballot box and supporting candidates who will pass safer gun laws. Join us:

body:
I’m ready to show up.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125562244/602185417/1239926708?refcode=ea.359037bb-190c-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ms=ea.359037bb-190c-f111-832e-0022482a9733&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNTkwMzdiYi0xOTBjLWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gOtiJ-J7E6OGwGbe07JWDZf9VMnaPEK8VYA3gg-UrNI=&emci=38839020-ef0b-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=359037bb-190c-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=51844520) [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125562247/602185422/1367290569?refcode=ea.359037bb-190c-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ms=ea.359037bb-190c-f111-832e-0022482a9733&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNTkwMzdiYi0xOTBjLWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gOtiJ-J7E6OGwGbe07JWDZf9VMnaPEK8VYA3gg-UrNI=) Hi there, it’s Phil. Before I ask you to **[chip in a few bucks to our grassroots movement for Colorado governor,](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125562252/602185426/1367290569?refcode=ea.359037bb-190c-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ms=ea.359037bb-190c-f111-832e-0022482a9733&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNTkwMzdiYi0xOTBjLWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gOtiJ-J7E6OGwGbe07JWDZf9VMnaPEK8VYA3gg-UrNI=)** I wanted to share something with you. Because you deserve to know why I’m asking you to invest in this campaign. You might’ve heard from me before about what a leader _doesn’t_ do. A leader _doesn’t_ try to appease bullies, like the President and his cabinet. A leader _doesn’t_ try to play ball with anyone whose obvious goal is to mistreat the people of our state. **I still believe that folding instead of fighting is the wrong strategy. It’s not what leaders do — not now, not ever.** But here’s the thing: by now, I’ve spent several years in Colorado state government, picking tough but worthwhile fights as your attorney general — and winning quite a few of them. This work has proven to me that it’s a hell of a lot easier to stand on the sidelines and complain than it is to _actually roll up your sleeves and get involved._ So in that spirit, here’s what an _effective_ leader does: **A leader takes a stand and doesn’t back down.** You might’ve heard of the idea that courage isn’t the absence of fear, it’s taking action in spite of it. Personally, I get my courage every day from the people of Colorado. I will never back down or give up on a worthwhile fight when the six million people of our state are relying on me. **A leader listens to and involves others.** The most valuable planks in our policy platform have always come from YOU — the people. It’s why we embarked on our first Fight for Colorado tour in October of last year. And it’s why we’re currently on another town hall tour all around our state. _I always want to hear directly from the people I have the privilege of representing._ **A leader doesn’t cave to pressure from the powerful, ultra-wealthy few.** This campaign will always prioritize putting the people of Colorado first, not billionaires or corporations. I will do the hard but important work of earning your trust, person by person. **A leader takes every opportunity to stand up for what’s right.** I’m the only candidate in this race who has taken every single opportunity to stand up to this lawless federal government. clean_body: I’m ready to show up. = Hi there, it’s Phil. Before I ask you to = I wanted to share something with you. Because you deserve to know why I’m asking you to invest in this campaign. You might’ve heard from me before about what a leader doesn’t do. A leader doesn’t try to appease bullies, like the President and his cabinet. A leader doesn’t try to play ball with anyone whose obvious goal is to mistreat the people of our state. I still believe that folding instead of fighting is the wrong strategy. It’s not what leaders do — not now, not ever. But here’s the thing: by now, I’ve spent several years in Colorado state government, picking tough but worthwhile fights as your attorney general — and winning quite a few of them. This work has proven to me that it’s a hell of a lot easier to stand on the sidelines and complain than it is to actually roll up your sleeves and get involved. So in that spirit, here’s what an effective leader does: A leader takes a stand and doesn’t back down. You might’ve heard of the idea that courage isn’t the absence of fear, it’s taking action in spite of it. Personally, I get my courage every day from the people of Colorado. I will never back down or give up on a worthwhile fight when the six million people of our state are relying on me. A leader listens to and involves others. The most valuable planks in our policy platform have always come from YOU — the people. It’s why we embarked on our first Fight for Colorado tour in October of last year. And it’s why we’re currently on another town hall tour all around our state. I always want to hear directly from the people I have the privilege of representing. A leader doesn’t cave to pressure from the powerful, ultra-wealthy few. This campaign will always prioritize putting the people of Colorado first, not billionaires or corporations. I will do the hard but important work of earning your trust, person by person. A leader takes every opportunity to stand up for what’s right. **One year ago today, I walked out of the Department of Justice rather than bow to Donald Trump’s corrupt demands.** I quit because I was ordered to drop a corruption case against former NY Mayor Eric Adams for unrelated political reasons. It was that simple, and that wrong. The DOJ's duty is to the law, not to Donald Trump's personal interests. Since that day, I've had one mission: **to help fix this broken system.** And let me tell you, traveling across PA-07 this past year has been the greatest privilege. I've met hundreds of you — in coffee shops, at factory gates, in our communities. You've shared your stories, your frustrations, and your hope. The message is clear: **we’re ready to turn the page on Donald Trump's corruption.** Now, we face our first real test. Starting today, we need to collect enough petition signatures to get on the May 19th primary ballot. Pulling this off requires a major push. We’re organizing volunteers across PA-07, printing materials to share with voters, and holding events across the district to gather thousands of signatures. * * *
Donald Trump and his MAGA cronies in this administration simply cannot help themselves when they see an opportunity to abuse the power of the federal government to silence their opposition.
Last night on CBS, Stephen Colbert was supposed to interview Texas Senate candidate James Talarico--one of the best Democratic candidates in the country this year. And Brendan Carr at the FCC and Bari Weiss at CBS stepped in and told Colbert he couldn't interview Talarico. Couldn't talk about him. Couldn't show an image of him. Couldn't even mention what was happening on air.
And like an employee who's two weeks from quitting and finally out of fucks to give, Stephen Colbert said: screw that.
He opened his show by calling out CBS and the FCC for trying to suppress a Democrat who dares stand up to Donald Trump. He called it what it is--blatant abuse of government power to control what he can and cannot say on his own show because they don't like his politics or his comedy. And then he had James Talarico on anyway.
They couldn't air it on CBS. So they put it on social media.
And in doing that, they created ten times more attention for the interview than it would've gotten if they'd just let it happen.
It was ethically wrong. It was politically brain-dead. It was an aggressively stupid move by the Trump administration, Bari Weiss, and CBS--to think they could silence someone as effective as Talarico, or tell someone as tough as Colbert what he can and cannot do with his own platform.
And it's not new.
* * *

* * *
They tried to get Jimmy Kimmel taken off the air over a joke. They arrested Don Lemon a few weeks ago. They've tried to sic a grand jury on six Democratic members of Congress over a video they didn't like. Time and again, they treat the Constitution like it's a subscription service: available for them, revoked for everyone else.
The First Amendment is for them.
The Second Amendment is for them.
The Constitution is for them.
For the rest of us? Apparently optional.
That's the pattern. It's what authoritarians do. They try to squash the press. They try to intimidate critics. The most dangerous part isn't even the overreach. It's the attempt to make the overreach feel normal.
Strip away the historical baggage and look at the textbook definition, and this is what scholars describe as fascistic behavior -- not in a World War II sense, but in structure. It's hostility toward dissent. It's using state power to pressure media institutions. It's treating political opposition as something to silence rather than debate. I know that word is deeply controversial among Trump supporters. But when government officials lean on regulators and corporations to suppress a critic because they don't like his politics, that's not normal partisan hardball. That's a governing style that rejects pluralism and punishes opposition. The goal is simple: make people scared to speak. Scared to protest. Scared to push back.
We can't be.
Because every single time they pull this shit, it backfires. And if they can do it to a late-night host on a major network, they can do it to anyone with a platform smaller and fewer lawyers.
In this case, they just handed James Talarico more attention than he could've bought with a seven-figure ad buy. And they did it weeks before a primary.
Let's be honest about why they targeted him. If Colbert had booked a Republican--or even a Democrat not running in one of the most competitive races in the country--no one would've blinked. But they're freaking out about Texas.
Texas is roughly Trump +10. But we're heading into an environment that could be anywhere from Democrats +8 to +15 nationally, because people are pissed about the economy. Talarico is exactly the kind of Democrat who can exploit that. He's won in Republican areas before. He can reach across the aisle. He's one of the most impressive communicators in the party.
And yes, he's running against Jasmine Crockett, who is impressive in her own right. Texas voters will decide their nominee in a few weeks. But this stunt? It boosted Talarico.
It reinforced his core message--that the billionaire class is trying to suppress anyone who challenges them.
One of my favorite lines from him came at a town hall recently, when someone accused him of pushing "class warfare" for going after the Epstein class. He said: "We already have class warfare in this country. Billionaires are waging war on the rest of us. We just need to tell the truth about it."
That's why they're scared.
Meanwhile, Republicans have created their own circus. Three candidates. Longtime incumbent John Cornyn bleeding support. A lieutenant governor in full MAGA cosplay. Another MAGA clone. The base wants the loudest, angriest option, not the one most likely to win a general election.
And when Trump had a chance to tip the scales toward the safer pick? Silence. The man has an opinion on everything except the race that actually matters.
So here's the setup: a Republican +10 state in a cycle where Republicans will be deeply unpopular, a Democratic candidate who can win crossover voters, and a potential GOP nominee who could depress turnout.
That's how you get a perfect storm.
And instead of playing it smart, they panic. They abuse power. They overreach. Like a rabid dog that's been starved for days, they lunge at the first thing they see without thinking about the consequences.
Now Talarico raises a ton of money off this. That money funds ads. Those ads spread his message. And he inches closer.
So sure--thank you.
I'd prefer they not abuse federal power at all. But if they're going to do it, at least keep doing it in spectacularly stupid ways. Because that's the defining feature of this administration: it's usually the most corrupt option available--and somehow also the dumbest.
We might actually be saved by their incompetence.
They don't know how to wield power strategically. They don't know how to keep the public on their side. That's why Trump's approval rating keeps sinking into the mid-30s.
We haven't hit bottom yet. People are still waking up. It's taken longer than I'd like--but I'll take them whenever they arrive.
In moments like this, we have to get louder.
Support Talarico or don't--that's your call. But every time Trump gets away with something small, he wants something bigger. It's "If You Give a Mouse a Cookie" politics (shoutout to my kiddo for making me read this 10,000 times when he was a toddler.) You give him an inch, he takes a mile. Then another. Then another.
You cannot give them anything.
When Don Lemon tells Trump to fuck off after being arrested? That's progress. When Stephen Colbert defies CBS and airs the interview anyway? That's solidarity.
That's a line in the sand.
So go find yours.
Figure out where you're willing to say "enough." Find a way to be useful. Keep pushing back.
Don't let the bastards grind you down.

Last night on CBS, Stephen Colbert was supposed to interview Texas Senate candidate James Talarico--one of the best Democratic candidates in the country this year. And Brendan Carr at the FCC and Bari Weiss at CBS stepped in and told Colbert he couldn't interview Talarico. Couldn't talk about him. Couldn't show an image of him. Couldn't even mention what was happening on air. And like an employee who's two weeks from quitting and finally out of fucks to give, Stephen Colbert said: screw that. He opened his show by calling out CBS and the FCC for trying to suppress a Democrat who dares stand up to Donald Trump. He called it what it is--blatant abuse of government power to control what he can and cannot say on his own show because they don't like his politics or his comedy. And then he had James Talarico on anyway. They couldn't air it on CBS. So they put it on social media. And in doing that, they created ten times more attention for the interview than it would've gotten if they'd just let it happen. It was ethically wrong. It was politically brain-dead. It was an aggressively stupid move by the Trump administration, Bari Weiss, and CBS--to think they could silence someone as effective as Talarico, or tell someone as tough as Colbert what he can and cannot do with his own platform. And it's not new. * They tried to get Jimmy Kimmel taken off the air over a joke. They arrested Don Lemon a few weeks ago. They've tried to sic a grand jury on six Democratic members of Congress over a video they didn't like. Time and again, they treat the Constitution like it's a subscription service: available for them, revoked for everyone else. The First Amendment is for them. The Second Amendment is for them. The Constitution is for them. For the rest of us? Apparently optional. That's the pattern. It's what authoritarians do. They try to squash the press. They try to intimidate critics. The most dangerous part isn't even the overreach. It's the attempt to make the overreach feel normal. Strip away the historical baggage and look at the textbook definition, and this is what scholars describe as fascistic behavior -- not in a World War II sense, but in structure. It's hostility toward dissent. It's using state power to pressure media institutions. It's treating political opposition as something to silence rather than debate. I know that word is deeply controversial among Trump supporters. But when government officials lean on regulators and corporations to suppress a critic because they don't like his politics, that's not normal partisan hardball. That's a governing style that rejects pluralism and punishes opposition. The goal is simple: make people scared to speak. Scared to protest. Scared to push back. We can't be. Because every single time they pull this shit, it backfires. And if they can do it to a late-night host on a major network, they can do it to anyone with a platform smaller and fewer lawyers. In this case, they just handed James Talarico more attention than he could've bought with a seven-figure ad buy. And they did it weeks before a primary. Let's be honest about why they targeted him. If Colbert had booked a Republican--or even a Democrat not running in one of the most competitive races in the country--no one would've blinked. But they're freaking out about Texas. Texas is roughly Trump +10. But we're heading into an environment that could be anywhere from Democrats +8 to +15 nationally, because people are pissed about the economy. Talarico is exactly the kind of Democrat who can exploit that. He's won in Republican areas before. He can reach across the aisle. He's one of the most impressive communicators in the party. And yes, he's running against Jasmine Crockett, who is impressive in her own right. Texas voters will decide their nominee in a few weeks. But this stunt? It boosted Talarico. It reinforced his core message--that the billionaire class is trying to suppress anyone who challenges them. One of my favorite lines from him came at a town hall recently, when someone accused him of pushing "class warfare" for going after the Epstein class. He said: "We already have class warfare in this country. Billionaires are waging war on the rest of us. We just need to tell the truth about it." That's why they're scared. Meanwhile, Republicans have created their own circus. Three candidates. Longtime incumbent John Cornyn bleeding support. A lieutenant governor in full MAGA cosplay. Another MAGA clone. The base wants the loudest, angriest option, not the one most likely to win a general election. And when Trump had a chance to tip the scales toward the safer pick? Silence. The man has an opinion on everything except the race that actually matters. So here's the setup: a Republican +10 state in a cycle where Republicans will be deeply unpopular, a Democratic candidate who can win crossover voters, and a potential GOP nominee who could depress turnout. That's how you get a perfect storm. And instead of playing it smart, they panic. They abuse power. They overreach. Like a rabid dog that's been starved for days, they lunge at the first thing they see without thinking about the consequences. Now Talarico raises a ton of money off this. That money funds ads. Those ads spread his message. And he inches closer. So sure--thank you. I'd prefer they not abuse federal power at all. But if they're going to do it, at least keep doing it in spectacularly stupid ways. Because that's the defining feature of this administration: it's usually the most corrupt option available--and somehow also the dumbest. We might actually be saved by their incompetence. They don't know how to wield power strategically. They don't know how to keep the public on their side. That's why Trump's approval rating keeps sinking into the mid-30s. We haven't hit bottom yet. People are still waking up. It's taken longer than I'd like--but I'll take them whenever they arrive. In moments like this, we have to get louder. Support Talarico or don't--that's your call. But every time Trump gets away with something small, he wants something bigger. It's "If You Give a Mouse a Cookie" politics (shoutout to my kiddo for making me read this 10,000 times when he was a toddler.) You give him an inch, he takes a mile. Then another. Then another. You cannot give them anything. When Don Lemon tells Trump to fuck off after being arrested? That's progress. When Stephen Colbert defies CBS and airs the interview anyway? That's solidarity. That's a line in the sand. So go find yours. Figure out where you're willing to say "enough." Find a way to be useful. Keep pushing back. Don't let the bastards grind you down. name: Ruben Gallego
subject: Housing
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
This is not a short email
#

**The housing crisis.**
I know these emails are supposed to be loud, bombastic, provoke outrage and get people to contribute... but this isn't going to be one of those emails.
This email is about housing, and how we tackle the crisis of countless Americans being unable to afford their first home.
I also know these emails are supposed to be short and punchy. Again, this isn't going to be one of those emails.
I am not going to share my entire 36 page housing plan, but I do want to share a summary written up by the Arizona Mirror for anyone who cares about this issue to consider.
**[Read the full article here.](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/3301?t=1&akid=4063%2E734936%2EOriiyM)**
Excerpts below.
* * *
**Build More Homes**
The first pillar of Gallego’s plan includes policy ideas aimed at creating more homes, citing the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program as a key place to invest.
The plan calls for strengthening and expanding private investment by making the LIHTC easier to use and establishing an “Extremely Low-Income Basis Boost” that Gallego says will “incentivize development in underserved areas.”
LIHTC has long been the main way the federal government finances affordable housing by offering tax credits to private investors for the creation of low-income housing. Developers of LIHTC properties must keep rents affordable for at least 30 years, but Gallego is also proposing an option for extending that to 50 years.
Gallego’s plan also includes tax credits for developers who convert old office buildings into residential or mixed-use properties that also dedicate a portion of the units to affordable housing.
And the Phoenix Democrat wants to expand financing options for homeowners who may want to build an accessory dwelling unit, also known as a casita, on their property.
Among a litany of other ideas, the plan also includes looking into using federal land for housing and repurposing federal property for housing.
**Clear the Path**
The Arizona Legislature has been mulling proposals to tackle the housing affordability crisis for several years, but with little success. Likewise, some municipalities have worked on policy changes aimed at increasing affordable housing, but with mixed results.
But Gallego wants to incentivize cities that are actively working to address the housing crisis by certifying jurisdictions that do so as “pro-housing,” opening up that community of homeowners and renters to rebates.
Those communities would be eligible for specialized federal grants, while municipalities that “persistently obstruct housing development” could “face accountability measures, such as reduced federal support,” according to Gallego’s plan.
Those jurisdictions would also get scores that would apply to transit-grant applications, which Gallego’s plan says would help prevent waste on federal transit funds and prioritize “investments where affordable housing and transit ridership can grow together.”
Gallego also wants to cut red tape around environmental reviews.
He wants to give the U.S. Housing and Urban Development’s environmental review delegation authority to states, local governments and tribal entities. He also wants HUD and the U.S. Department of Agriculture to conduct environmental reviews for housing projects that receive money from both of them to do them together, to reduce costs and the delay on projects.
**Lower Housing Costs**
The plan also includes ideas on how to make home ownership more attainable.
As the prices of houses have skyrocketed over the past two decades, more younger people are being priced out of purchasing homes, forcing them instead to rent. Gallego wants to lower the Federal Housing Administration’s down payment requirements from 3.5% to either zero or 1% for first-time homebuyers “who struggle to save but demonstrate reliable rent payment history.”
Gallego is also calling for a federal home loan program for teachers and first responders that would come out of the FHA and would be eligible to law enforcement, firefighters, EMTs, paramedics and teachers who are first time home buyers.
Like many other Democrats, Gallego is also proposing a continued crackdown on price-fixing and rent manipulation schemes by companies like RealPage.
**Future-proof Homes**
The last pillar of Gallego’s plan revolves around climate change and how the country’s new and existing housing stock needs to adapt to the ongoing threats around it.
One study has estimated that climate change will cause a $1.47 trillion decline in home values in the United States by 2055.
Gallego’s plan seeks to mitigate some of that by suggesting that money canceled by the Trump administration be reinstated. It also aims to invest in homes that are doing weatherization and energy efficiency upgrades, such as adding insulation, sealing windows and wrapping water pipes.
The plan also suggests deducting home insurance from federal taxes and incentivizing states to require home insurance discounts for mitigation efforts. Insurance companies have begun descending upon Arizona with new technology in the wake of extreme weather in recent months to perform risk assessments which could lead to higher rates.
* * *
Semper Fi,
Ruben

### From Indiana Mom to US Congresswoman
---

| | On this episode of the Moms for America Podcast, Debbie welcomes US Representative Erin Houchin for a candid conversation about balancing motherhood and public service. From school schedules to committee hearings, Rep. Houchin shares what it looks like to juggle family life while fighting for her constituents and conservative values in Washington. # DNC Louisiana v. Callais Stakeholder Briefing
---
| |
The Democratic National Committee (DNC) invites you to a special virtual briefing on [**Thursday, February 19th, at 8:00 PM ET**](https://collegedems.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b3a52587106e5f265f227782b&id=a4d348973c&e=d6c5c7d7ec) on the stakes of [ _Louisiana v. Callais_](https://collegedems.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b3a52587106e5f265f227782b&id=93b3967163&e=d6c5c7d7ec) , one of the most critical Supreme Court cases in years.
This landmark case is part of an ongoing battle against Trump and his conservative allies’ efforts in the South and across the country to redraw Congressional districts to deny Black and Brown voters meaningful representation.**** The strength and survival of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act is central to protecting communities of color from gerrymandering and at-large elections that dilute their voting power and rig the system.

**JOIN US TO :**
* Learn how we got here
* Understand why this case matters and its broader impact on communities and the 2026 elections
* Gain critical information to inform your networks and partners

body:
#

**I’m sorry about Karoline Leavitt.**
A few years ago, Karoline Leavitt ran against me for Congress here in New Hampshire. Her campaign was steeped in extreme MAGA rhetoric and zero connection to the actual issues Granite Staters face every day. **Voters saw right through it and rejected her agenda by nearly 10 points**. [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=partner_ms_cp_em_slotkin_em2510227&refcode2=2414.135344.zCqp7u&t=1&akid=2414%2E135344%2EzCqp7u)
---
Unfortunately that race turned into a national audition. Now the same talking points and spin that New Hampshire voters dismissed are being used daily from the White House briefing room.
So if you’re wondering how the rest of the country ended up having to listen to Karoline Leavitt, it’s because New Hampshire proved something important first: Her extreme ideas don’t hold up when you put them in front of real voters.
But that hasn’t stopped the MAGA machine from trying. **National Republicans are pouring money into New Hampshire because they think they can break through and notch a win here to cling to their Senate majority**. They’ve lined up behind John Sununu, an NRSC-backed candidate who will vote with Donald Trump and MAGA leadership when it matters most. It’s a new candidate reading from the same old playbook.
I’ve beaten their playbook before by focusing on kitchen-table issues, standing up for families, and telling the truth. Now I need your help to do it again. [**Will you split a contribution between me and Elissa Slotkin today to help us keep this Senate seat blue and fight for what matters to Granite Staters? **](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=partner_ms_cp_em_slotkin_em2510227&t=2&akid=2414%2E135344%2EzCqp7u)
Granite Staters value independence. They reward common sense. And they don’t like being sold a script written somewhere else.
If you believe New Hampshire should keep leading the way and showing the rest of the country that MAGA politics don’t work here, I’m asking you to be a part of our campaign. **If Democrats are going to flip the Senate, we need to win this open race in New Hampshire.**
[**Will you split a donation today between my campaign and Elissa Slotkin to help us keep this Senate seat blue and stop national Republicans from installing another vote for Trump’s agenda? **](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=partner_ms_cp_em_slotkin_em2510227&t=3&akid=2414%2E135344%2EzCqp7u)

name: Justin Riemer - RITE President
subject: RITE Urges Supreme Court to Affirm Meaning of Election Day
body:
Confident SCOTUS will affirm that mail ballots must be returned by Election Day |
---
| |
---
| | **RITE Urges Supreme Court to Affirm Meaning of Election Day**
**WASHINGTON, DC** – Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect the rule of law in elections, has filed its [second amicus brief](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=965281aea1&e=ea91f782ea) with the United States Supreme Court in support of plaintiffs in _Watson v. Republican National Committee_. RITE filed the brief jointly with the Center for Election Confidence, Honest Elections Project, and the American Legislative Exchange Council.

The case asks whether federal law establishing a single, uniform Election Day preempts state laws that allow mail-in ballots to be received and counted after Election Day. The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals held that Mississippi’s post–Election Day ballot receipt deadline conflicts with federal statutes requiring that federal elections occur on one day nationwide. RITE asks the Court to affirm the Fifth Circuit’s decision. RITE, CEC, and HEP previously filed an [amicus brief](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=9ecf8ec91b&e=ea91f782ea) with the Supreme Court at the certiorari petition stage, helping persuade the Court to accept the case. The Court will hear oral argument on March 23, 2026.

“Congress spoke clearly about the meaning of Election Day. We are confident that the Supreme Court will affirm that it means ballots must be returned by that date,” said RITE President Justin Riemer. "An Election Day deadline is not only legally required, it also helps ensure order and confidence in our elections. RITE is proud to stand with Center for Election Confidence, Honest Elections Project, and ALEC in urging the Court to enforce the plain meaning of federal law.”
###
