* **Juliana fights for the people.** She has spent her career in service of others — first as her mother was navigating the healthcare system during her battle with Alzheimer’s and saw firsthand how broken the system was. Then, she took that fight head on as a state representative after defeating a 13-year incumbent. Today, as lieutenant governor, she's standing for all Illinoisans, and making sure they have what they need to thrive in their state.
* **Juliana is no stranger to breaking barriers.** As the first Black woman to serve as lieutenant governor of Illinois, Juliana has broken barriers and opened doors. But she's never forgotten where she came from or who she's fighting for, and she has the courage and vision to deliver real results in the Senate.
* **Juliana has a clear vision for progress.** As Donald Trump pushes an agenda that raises costs for working families to benefit the ultra-wealthy, Juliana has a plan to fight for the people of Illinois. Her blueprint for making life more affordable includes quality healthcare, a little more money in your pocket, and a government that has all Americans in mind.

| | _**CLICK ABOVE IMAGE TO WATCH EPISODE **_
---
| | **Is Jesus really first in our lives? Many professed Christians will say yes, but when it comes to politics, many rebel against Biblically defined morality in the name of politics. Whether it’s to satisfy their own political aspirations, to appease the political collective or tribe they are loyal to. Scripture tells us in Ephesians 5:11, “Have nothing to do with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them.” **
****
**Proverbs 24:11-12 "Rescue those being led away to death; hold back those staggering toward slaughter. If you say, “But we knew nothing about this,” does not he who weighs the heart perceive it?"Does not he who guards your life know it? Will he not repay everyone according to what they have done?"**
****
**What Jesus expects of us comes FIRST in all areas of life, including our political activities. When we, as Christians in politics, participate in or turn a blind eye to things God calls wicked, we are just as complicit in the destruction of America as Marxists and the globalist-cult. Matthew 5:13-16 Jesus tells us we are to be salt and light, and if we lose our saltiness or hide our light under a lamp, we are useless. Additionally, we are being hypocritical and actually harming efforts to spread the Gospel, as professed Christians if we are complicit in evil Christ rebukes. Everything in life must be in submission to God’s mission.**
****
**Caleb Collier of Church and State ([churchandstate.media](https://link.kristinakaramo.com/campaigns/vp560896g8daa/track-url/rb99335sg3c36/f4e6309ba1f69d1b056312ac0b2845aa5464e679)) has worn many hats in politics. He has served as a member of the Spokane Valley, Washington, city council, worked for the John Birch Society and Turning Point USA, and is a Marine veteran. He now runs Church and State media to help improve the situational awareness of Christians in America. Reminding Christians that, irrespective of political turmoil, our primary duty is to Christ and that heaven is ultimately our home. Visit [Church And State | Discover the Church And State Podcast](https://link.kristinakaramo.com/campaigns/vp560896g8daa/track-url/rb99335sg3c36/b08c44a819e026c689f82b1ae8041885bb7e1904)**

**To God Alone be the Glory,****Kristina Karamo**

Team,
Trump is pushing to “nationalize” elections and end mail-in voting in his effort to “stop noncitizen voting”, despite **no proof of substantial noncitizen voting.** The Republican SAVE America Act is the next way he’s trying to do that.
The SAVE America Act is a Republican bill that will require proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. It would require bringing proof, such as a passport, REAL ID, or a physical birth certificate, to the polls.
This kind of proof can be very difficult to provide. Over 21 million Americans lack easy access to those documents. Roughly half of all Americans don’t have a passport and cannot get one because of the cost. And millions of Americans lack access to a physical copy of their birth certificate.
**It’s a direct attack on our Democracy.**

| | Hello, Friend, I hope you're doing well today. I'm reaching out to share something that's been on my mind lately...

Are you as concerned about the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) as I am? Many Americans are--and for good reason.

While AI-powered chatbots and search engines can be quite helpful, artificial intelligence can also be used in harmful and even deadly ways.

For example, in the war between Russia and Ukraine, both countries are utilizing AI in an effort to make their drones and other weapons more and more deadly.

And in China, the ruling Communist Party uses AI to control its population, which enables China to punish dissidents and reward loyalists more effectively.

**In other words, AI, like every other technology, can be used for good or for ill. **

As American citizens, our task is to ensure that AI technology is used to preserve rather than to destroy freedom.

That's why Hillsdale College created a free online video series to help you understand what AI means for our future--and our freedom.

This fascinating, FREE online video series examines artificial intelligence, including its relationship to human nature, the threat it poses to self-government, and its uses on the battlefield.

**You can receive instant access to our free AI-video teaching series right now using this secure link: **

[**https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-colleges-artificial-intelligence-video-series**](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/k8kXkcSk_-6hqK-ReQqV4VrDihXiTQAClgsc6BLhMV1nNaWP7EOuv53KJG5-Lp8BC1kRJwwbC8pV2eKn7NKfnXLk8z8dev5_DVYgOu39eQr8sfXOr0WUfawqvCbVnqAtM7209ofwtOQUxnftXPBQYixuY24jYXtI2dlJn0eN1Uk5FeVncgdJn_9CaZV9tFJsFirUYLjZzzvSSLm8LdsQvcqcIN_3FkuHWdRIwCBw8U4Tr4DMcb8MVzDzUhVcM35m1GtqnvTuOvub2ZCaAeKXsZZD851oO01wsQRYEardCGdEb30I1RUQ9STNmekGuFySz8N2UmPkhTPW-nO_pfd6YGbO461q2OZKT9Iv7L5FzhJ-J6ng-hRyhaqmV673ww3G9AnQOPLePttbJmMVJSQTAGBh4dvoaiwM1tkdIi97FaGfVOkg1td6zfa6hhEO2BHg8uKrVV9DSoyZar6Jq6Slof5BilEHh8VyAiv3isNKIe3F5TpKfpEFRo9ZhhIo-EMbSDCyDU9WB-X7zC0qKSPKjP6IbuIiZEUt97rWKy-lKb4D5BTVVCJVjK2rel6s-35uxlEwsh3LWKdCvWAnaLI7c0es1TcsVjBiwM_JODhrmESL7qR4ObB_1smZsFE-1oUU8KQP_iLhsb8p0nE2c0WB0ht_FjKYG6fA3UGF3DUns-jQAmfiG0ZcohR2vmVYRSyNrlnwO7GKGijxlTVpD1pQH6afU9RW1evJpNAjkqX6pOkVynaIPqWswDT6x9UiAQy9R5JmbTzDS619_6T0Ig/dPiEBXjbKnom3ietTvwVCScrgNVoZITd/17)

Friend, as self-governing citizens, we should learn about the opportunities--and the dangers--of artificial intelligence.

I hope you'll take a few minutes today to start watching. It's free, and I think you'll find it both eye-opening and encouraging.

Warm regards,

Bill Gray, '01

Peter, This weekend, I was invited to attend the Munich Security Conference, where leaders from around the world are gathered to talk about the future of democracy, security, climate, and economic stability. **And I’ll be honest: the damage done to America’s credibility over the past year is real. That’s the message I shared on my panel. ** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125581669/602251173/1740130687?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260217_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyY2UyMWM4OC0zZTBjLWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=itbXGKpLqHBodfEDoo-dUwnnL5AKnfWtjLg8FNnsCH8=) [**If you’re short on time today but are standing with me in the work to take back the House and restore U.S. credibility globally, pitch in right now.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125581670/602251174/1740130687?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260217_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyY2UyMWM4OC0zZTBjLWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=itbXGKpLqHBodfEDoo-dUwnnL5AKnfWtjLg8FNnsCH8=) | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125581671/602251175/1740130687?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260217_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyY2UyMWM4OC0zZTBjLWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=itbXGKpLqHBodfEDoo-dUwnnL5AKnfWtjLg8FNnsCH8=)

Allies are questioning our strength. Young people across the globe are wondering whether democracy can still deliver. And at home, an entire generation is losing faith in a political and economic system that too often feels like it wasn’t built for us.
It will take a lot of work to rebuild trust in the United States — and it won’t happen overnight. But we _can_ rebuild it.
I’ve spent my career working on global climate agreements and international partnerships. I’ve seen firsthand what American leadership can accomplish when we show up with seriousness, integrity, and a commitment to shared progress. I also know how quickly that leadership can erode when we abandon our values.
**Right now, the Trump administration’s reckless approach has weakened our standing abroad and deepened cynicism at home.**
The modest support Trump was able to get from some young voters in 2024 is evaporating.
As the youngest woman serving in Congress, I hear it everywhere I go: young people are demanding bold, transformational change.
**If we want to rebuild U.S. leadership around the world, we must take back the House.**
That’s why I’m asking: [**will you donate today to support my work in Congress and help flip the House?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125581672/602251176/1740130687?refcode=AU_YA_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260217_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyY2UyMWM4OC0zZTBjLWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=itbXGKpLqHBodfEDoo-dUwnnL5AKnfWtjLg8FNnsCH8=)
The work to rebuild credibility, at home and abroad, won’t be easy. But I believe deeply in this country. I believe in the next generation. And I believe that with bold leadership and a strong grassroots movement, we can restore faith in democracy and deliver the transformational change people are demanding.
Thank you for being part of this fight.

Peter,
At this point, dismantling ICE is the moderate position.
It is time to unmask these thugs. Arrest them. Haul them – and especially their leadership – in front of congressional committees and make them answer for these horrors.
I get told a lot that I don’t mince words. That it is “refreshing” for a politician to talk the way I do and to say what we’re all already thinking.
In the Senate, I’m not going to express “concern” like Susan Collins, and I’m not going to be another mealy-mouthed corporate Democrat either.
There are masked, secret police kidnapping and murdering people on the streets of America. It’s time we start talking and acting like it.
I am running for the U.S. Senate to defeat Susan Collins here in Maine because we need to replace Collins with a Democrat who is actually ready to fight like hell to defend our country against fascism.

## A long overdue win for American health
For years, the media and the establishment laughed at anyone who dared question the safety of food dyes, artificial sweeteners, and thousands of other additives slipped into our grocery aisles.
"Generally Recognized as Safe" -- GRAS -- was the magic phrase that let Big Food and Big Ag decide for themselves what's okay to feed us.
No rigorous FDA review. No real oversight.
Just a self-certification that "experts" (often paid by the companies) say it's fine.
The whole thing never really passed the smell test.
Red dye No. 3? Banned in cosmetics because it causes cancer in lab animals, but still in our candy and soda.
Titanium dioxide? Pulled from candy in Europe over DNA damage concerns, but still here.
The list goes on.
Americans have been eating these chemicals for decades while the media mocked anyone who asked why.
But thanks to HHS Secretary RFK, that's changing.
Let's break it down...

subject: We have an opportunity to explore what a world would look like if we upheld democracy, human rights, trade that actually centers working-class people instead of accruing overwhelmingly the benefits of trade to the wealthiest.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
This past Friday, at the Munich Security Conference, someone asked me, “Do you think we’re in a new world order?”
Prime Minister Carney’s remarks at the World Economic Forum were words that rang around the world in raising this question.
But I think that also in his remarks, as well as part of this larger conversation, there was this undertone, this undercurrent, this suggestion, that it was a rules based order _sometimes._
And I think that is the issue that lies before us. That in a so-called “rules based order,” the rules for whom? Because for all too long, the rules only applied to the United States, Europe, its allies and we would carve out exceptions for the Global South.
When you have a rules based order where you carve out exceptions to our values, exceptions to our rules — eventually the exceptions become the rules.
Over the last 5 years we've seen such a breaking and such a fraying of these alleged western values that people wonder if it ever existed in the first place.
So I don't know if it's necessarily that we are in a post-rules based order. I think it’s possible we were in a pre-rules based order.
**We have an opportunity to explore what a world would look like if we upheld democracy, human rights, trade that actually centers working-class people instead of accruing overwhelmingly the benefits of trade to the wealthiest.**
If we reoriented to a new era, that could actually help people and show how foreign policy and healthy foreign policy can show up and help them in their lives.

* * *
_**By Eric J. Lullove, DPM**_
In the modern landscape of American healthcare, the bridge between a physician's prescription pad and a patient's pharmacy counter is no longer a direct path. It is a toll road, governed by _**Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs).**_ While these entities were originally designed to streamline drug delivery and negotiate lower prices, the current reality in 2026 is far more complex--and for many patients, far more dangerous.
As a physician in private practice, I see the human cost of these "administrative" decisions every day. When a PBM denies a specific wound care therapy or a life-altering specialty medication, they aren't just managing a formulary; they are actively altering the trajectory of a patient's life.
### Market Concentration and Pricing Dynamics
To understand the problem, we must first look at the sheer scale of market dominance. A staggering **79% of all prescription drug claims** in the United States are controlled by just three entities: **CVS Caremark (33%), Express Scripts (24%), and OptumRx (22%).** When you expand that to the top six PBMs, they handle **96% of the market.**
This extreme concentration has raised significant concerns about limited competition, prompting a series of Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigations. The core issue is a "high-list-price/high-rebate" incentive structure. When PBMs retain percentages of rebates, they often prefer expensive drugs that generate larger "kickbacks" over lower-cost alternatives that would save patients money.
> **The Rebate Gap:** Between 2011 and 2016, rebates and payments from manufacturers to intermediaries increased **15% annually** , while net revenues for those drugs grew by only **2.7%**.
> [The Basics of PBM](https://substack.com/redirect/29c82fe9-a5dd-46bc-b013-1cd48f6a1070?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.3XkzCRy5nhjVuLhmRh2SiChaeEJf_twRIo4hcgpeRvs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=188306413)
### The Clinical Cost of "Utilization Management"
We often hear the terms "Prior Authorization" (PA) and "Step Therapy" (the "fail-first" requirement) framed as quality control. In practice, they often serve as barriers to medically necessary care, with devastating effects on outcomes.
#### 1\. Medication Adherence
The strongest evidence base in this field relates to adherence. A systematic review of 93 studies found that **68.3% of medication adherence outcomes** showed negative correlations with formulary restrictions. In plain terms: when we make it harder for patients to get their medicine through red tape and high costs, they stop taking it.
#### 2\. Clinical Outcomes in Multiple Sclerosis
A 2025 study in _JAMA Network Open_ examined formulary exclusions for MS medications in Medicare Part D, finding that beneficiaries' access was restricted on an average of **45% of brand-only compounds**. For heterogeneous conditions like MS, where treatment effects vary wildly across patients, these exclusions are associated with increased relapse episodes and disease progression.
#### 3\. Specialty Drugs and Socioeconomic Vulnerability
The burden falls heaviest on our most vulnerable. For specialty medications, increasing cost-sharing above **$100** was associated with up to **75% abandonment rates**. Lower-income patients experience the worst outcomes, while those with complex neurologic or autoimmune diseases face missed doses and increased emergency department visits due to therapy delays.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=188306413&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg4MzA2NDEzLCJpYXQiOjE3NzEzNjYwNDAsImV4cCI6MTc3Mzk1ODA0MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.UN_JYfhKcWCx2JgaHkpXnNmVxOKVkd4DaBsCY2o7QDM)
### Policy in Motion: Government Intervention and the 2026 Reform Wave
The administration has shifted from monitoring to active intervention on the "back end" of the PBM model. In early 2026, the **Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (CAA 2026)** was signed into law, representing a decisive strike against these "middleman" incentives.
#### Combatting the "Black Box"
The federal government has recently taken several steps to accelerate the dismantling of PBM profit-taking:
* **Mandatory Rebate Pass-Through:** PBMs are now required to remit **100% of rebates** to the health plan sponsors, ending the practice of "rebate skimming."
* **Delinking in Medicare Part D:** PBM compensation is now "delinked" from drug list prices. They must be paid via **flat, fair-market fees** for service, removing the incentive to prefer high-priced drugs.
* **FTC Settlements:** In February 2026, the FTC secured a landmark settlement following investigations into major PBMs, requiring fundamental changes to their business practices to drive down insulin costs and increase transparency for all products.

[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=188306413&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg4MzA2NDEzLCJpYXQiOjE3NzEzNjYwNDAsImV4cCI6MTc3Mzk1ODA0MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.UN_JYfhKcWCx2JgaHkpXnNmVxOKVkd4DaBsCY2o7QDM&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
### The Inflation Reduction Act: Impact Beyond Medicare
One of the most debated pieces of legislation is the **Inflation Reduction Act (IRA)**. While famous for allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices, its effects are rippling through the entire American economy--both positively and adversely for those not on Medicare.
#### The Positive Spillover
* **The "Shaming" Effect on Insulin:** While the IRA's $35 insulin cap only applied to Medicare, the political and market pressure forced major manufacturers to voluntarily extend that cap to the **private sector**.
* **Inflation Penalties:** The IRA penalizes manufacturers who raise prices faster than inflation. Because these penalties are calculated based on national averages, it creates a "price ceiling" that helps slow cost increases for commercial insurance premiums as well.

#### The Adverse Consequences
* **Cost-Shifting to Private Plans:** As manufacturers lose margin in the Medicare segment due to negotiation, there is a risk they will seek to recoup that revenue by **raising prices on new drugs** for the commercial market.
* **Increased "Red Tape":** PBMs, seeing their Medicare profit margins squeezed by the new "delinking" rules, have doubled down on **utilization management** in the private sector. Patients on employer-sponsored plans are now seeing _more_ prior authorizations and _stricter_ step therapy as PBMs pivot their revenue strategies.

### Conclusion: A Market in Transition
The evidence shows that PBM restrictions directly harm medication adherence and clinical outcomes. While the administration's recent 2026 reforms and the IRA are finally introducing transparency and price controls, we are in a volatile transition period.
As a physician, my priority remains the patient in front of me. We must continue to advocate for a system where clinical endpoints--not rebate percentages--dictate care.

Unmasking the Middlemen: Why Your Prescription Price Has Little to Do With the Cost of the Drug | | and | Feb 17 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. By Eric J. Lullove, DPM In the modern landscape of American healthcare, the bridge between a physician's prescription pad and a patient's pharmacy counter is no longer a direct path. It is a toll road, governed by Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs). While these entities were originally designed to streamline drug delivery and negotiate lower prices, the current reality in 2026 is far more complex--and for many patients, far more dangerous. As a physician in private practice, I see the human cost of these "administrative" decisions every day. When a PBM denies a specific wound care therapy or a life-altering specialty medication, they aren't just managing a formulary; they are actively altering the trajectory of a patient's life. Market Concentration and Pricing Dynamics To understand the problem, we must first look at the sheer scale of market dominance. A staggering 79% of all prescription drug claims in the United States are controlled by just three entities: CVS Caremark (33%), Express Scripts (24%), and OptumRx (22%). When you expand that to the top six PBMs, they handle 96% of the market. This extreme concentration has raised significant concerns about limited competition, prompting a series of Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigations. The core issue is a "high-list-price/high-rebate" incentive structure. When PBMs retain percentages of rebates, they often prefer expensive drugs that generate larger "kickbacks" over lower-cost alternatives that would save patients money. The Rebate Gap: Between 2011 and 2016, rebates and payments from manufacturers to intermediaries increased 15% annually , while net revenues for those drugs grew by only 2.7%. The Clinical Cost of "Utilization Management" We often hear the terms "Prior Authorization" (PA) and "Step Therapy" (the "fail-first" requirement) framed as quality control. In practice, they often serve as barriers to medically necessary care, with devastating effects on outcomes. 1\. Medication Adherence The strongest evidence base in this field relates to adherence. A systematic review of 93 studies found that 68.3% of medication adherence outcomes showed negative correlations with formulary restrictions. In plain terms: when we make it harder for patients to get their medicine through red tape and high costs, they stop taking it. 2\. Clinical Outcomes in Multiple Sclerosis A 2025 study in JAMA Network Open examined formulary exclusions for MS medications in Medicare Part D, finding that beneficiaries' access was restricted on an average of 45% of brand-only compounds. For heterogeneous conditions like MS, where treatment effects vary wildly across patients, these exclusions are associated with increased relapse episodes and disease progression. 3\. Specialty Drugs and Socioeconomic Vulnerability The burden falls heaviest on our most vulnerable. For specialty medications, increasing cost-sharing above $100 was associated with up to 75% abandonment rates. Lower-income patients experience the worst outcomes, while those with complex neurologic or autoimmune diseases face missed doses and increased emergency department visits due to therapy delays. Policy in Motion: Government Intervention and the 2026 Reform Wave The administration has shifted from monitoring to active intervention on the "back end" of the PBM model. In early 2026, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (CAA 2026) was signed into law, representing a decisive strike against these "middleman" incentives. Combatting the "Black Box" The federal government has recently taken several steps to accelerate the dismantling of PBM profit-taking: Mandatory Rebate Pass-Through: PBMs are now required to remit 100% of rebates to the health plan sponsors, ending the practice of "rebate skimming." Delinking in Medicare Part D: PBM compensation is now "delinked" from drug list prices. They must be paid via flat, fair-market fees for service, removing the incentive to prefer high-priced drugs. FTC Settlements: In February 2026, the FTC secured a landmark settlement following investigations into major PBMs, requiring fundamental changes to their business practices to drive down insulin costs and increase transparency for all products. The Inflation Reduction Act: Impact Beyond Medicare One of the most debated pieces of legislation is the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). While famous for allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices, its effects are rippling through the entire American economy--both positively and adversely for those not on Medicare. The Positive Spillover The "Shaming" Effect on Insulin: While the IRA's $35 insulin cap only applied to Medicare, the political and market pressure forced major manufacturers to voluntarily extend that cap to the private sector. Inflation Penalties: The IRA penalizes manufacturers who raise prices faster than inflation. Because these penalties are calculated based on national averages, it creates a "price ceiling" that helps slow cost increases for commercial insurance premiums as well. The Adverse Consequences Cost-Shifting to Private Plans: As manufacturers lose margin in the Medicare segment due to negotiation, there is a risk they will seek to recoup that revenue by raising prices on new drugs for the commercial market. Increased "Red Tape": PBMs, seeing their Medicare profit margins squeezed by the new "delinking" rules, have doubled down on utilization management in the private sector. Patients on employer-sponsored plans are now seeing more prior authorizations and stricter step therapy as PBMs pivot their revenue strategies. Conclusion: A Market in Transition The evidence shows that PBM restrictions directly harm medication adherence and clinical outcomes. While the administration's recent 2026 reforms and the IRA are finally introducing transparency and price controls, we are in a volatile transition period. As a physician, my priority remains the patient in front of me. We must continue to advocate for a system where clinical endpoints--not rebate percentages--dictate care. Dr. Lullove is the Chief Executive and Medical Officer of the West Boca Center for Wound Healing in Coconut Creek, FL. I'm running for office as a Constituent, not a Politician

You’re receiving this Newsletter because you have donated to our campaign, you have requested information from our campaign, or you are a supporter of Tracy’s and therefore a friend of our campaign. No matter how you found us, we are happy you are here! This campaign is built upon the foundation of:
* ending the “us versus them” divisiveness;
* restoring the Checks & Balances that our Constitution requires and that our current Congress has abandoned; and
* steering our government back toward Democracy, where We the People give direction to our elected representatives, not the other way around.

# Campaign Updates
|
---
**February 17 – March 10:** We are quickly approaching what is known as Petition Signing! In short, our campaign needs to collect 1,000 unique signatures of registered Democrats who live in this Congressional District (PA-01). For those who are not sure, PA-01 consists of all of Bucks County and a small portion of Montgomery County. (We can help you determine if you’re in the District, just email us at: [tph@hunt4congress.com](mailto:tph@hunt4congress.com)). So, if you live in the (PA-01) District, please reach out to us so that we can have someone bring you a Petition to sign. They have to be signed in person on an official Petition form. Also, if you know other registered Democrats who live in the District, please reach out to them and see if they will sign as well. **IMPORTANT:** This is not a vote for me, this is not an endorsement of me and this is not a financial commitment to me; it is simply a signature saying that you believe I should be on the ballot for the May 19, 2026 Democratic Primary. ***Petition Signing Event*** Wednesday 2/18 from 5-7pm Triumph Restaurant & Brewery 400 Union Square Drive New Hope, PA 18938 **A few other updates:** There are now 7 Democratic candidates running for the May Primary!...The Montgomery County Democratic Committee is holding their Endorsement Meeting on February 18, 2026 and the Bucks County Democratic Committee is holding its Endorsement Meeting on February 21, 2026....While we are not expecting to receive either committee’s endorsement since we are not part of the “establishment”, we are hoping that neither party will endorse a particular candidate and that the voters of PA-01 will get to decide for themselves who they would like to support without having a thumb on the scale from the Party bosses.

|
---
**February 26 –** The Business Club, 400 Mill Street, Bristol, PA. This will be a Candidates Town Hall style event with multiple Democratic candidates answering questions from the voters. The Town Hall will run from 6:30p.m. – 9:00p.m., with a social gathering immediately thereafter for further discussion with the candidates. **March 9 –** Bucks County Community College, Epstein Campus at Lower Bucks, 1304 Veterans Hwy, Bristol, PA. This Candidates Town Hall will be part of the College’s Civics Series. It will follow the same Town Hall format of questions from the voters. This event will take place during the daytime so as to allow students on campus to attend.

IMPORTANT: This is not a vote for me, this is not an endorsement of me and this is not a financial commitment to me; it is simply a signature saying that you believe I should be on the ballot for the May 19, 2026 Democratic Primary. Petition Signing Event Wednesday 2/18 from 5-7pm Triumph Restaurant & Brewery 400 Union Square Drive New Hope, PA 18938 A few other updates: There are now 7 Democratic candidates running for the May Primary!...The Montgomery County Democratic Committee is holding their Endorsement Meeting on February 18, 2026 and the Bucks County Democratic Committee is holding its Endorsement Meeting on February 21, 2026....While we are not expecting to receive either committee’s endorsement since we are not part of the “establishment”, we are hoping that neither party will endorse a particular candidate and that the voters of PA-01 will get to decide for themselves who they would like to support without having a thumb on the scale from the Party bosses. | | | | Where You Will Find Me | February 26 – The Business Club, 400 Mill Street, Bristol, PA. This will be a Candidates Town Hall style event with multiple Democratic candidates answering questions from the voters. The Town Hall will run from 6:30p.m. – 9:00p.m., with a social gathering immediately thereafter for further discussion with the candidates. March 9 – Bucks County Community College, Epstein Campus at Lower Bucks, 1304 Veterans Hwy, Bristol, PA. This Candidates Town Hall will be part of the College’s Civics Series. It will follow the same Town Hall format of questions from the voters. This event will take place during the daytime so as to allow students on campus to attend. | | | | | Donate To continue to get the word out about our campaign and to connect with as many folks as possible here in PA-01, we constantly need marketing materials of all types which ain’t cheap!! Any financial support you can offer is greatly appreciated. Simply click the button below or go to: | | | | | | Update your Voter Registration | Note regarding the Deadline: 05/04/2026 is the last day to register before the 05/19/2026 election. | | | | | | | | | | | | Congressional Candidate Tracy P Hunt** | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Tracy Hunt for Congress You received this email because you signed up on our website or donated to the campaign.

**American healthcare reacts to crises, rather than prevent them**
_When patients control resources, healthcare system work for them, rather than around them._
**By** Charles Sauer

* * *

Healthcare is intensely personal, and when devastating news arrives in the exam room, lives and families are changed in an instant. Yet a system bogged down by regulation and bureaucracy too often compounds that pain, forcing patients to navigate the most frightening chapter of their lives alone. We must change that.
That’s why President Trump’s plan to fund patients – not the system – is revolutionary. Shifting power from government bureaucrats, insurance companies, and big hospital systems will allow Americans to make their own healthcare decisions. When patients control the resources, the healthcare system begins to work for them rather than around them.
Today, one of the clearest examples of why this approach matters is Alzheimer’s disease.
In a powerful **[Wall Street Journal op-ed](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)** , Dr. Brent Beasley recounts how he was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s at age 57 after losing his job due to unexplained cognitive struggles. Despite being a physician with significant medical knowledge and strong connections, securing a diagnosis took nearly a year – precious time when early intervention can make a life-changing difference.
But Dr. Beasley’s story is not one of despair. It’s one of hope.
Because his disease was detected early enough, his care team successfully intervened. Treatment helped him regain clarity, remain active in his church, and live a purposeful life. His experience is deeply encouraging. You can read his story **[here](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)**.
**An Alzheimer’s diagnosis no longer has to mean immediate decline.**
Science is opening doors that did not exist a decade ago. Yet Dr. Beasley’s story demonstrates that America’s healthcare system is largely designed to react to crises rather than prevent them. Patients are often diagnosed too late even though early interventions and lifestyle changes can have profound impacts.
Removing barriers to early testing, expanding access to innovative treatments, and supporting caregivers must become a national priority.
There is another reason policymakers should pay attention.
Analysts, including President Trump’s former Domestic Policy Advisor Joe Grogan and Paragon Research Fellow Ryan Long, increasingly **[warn that Alzheimer’s is not only a medical challenge but an economic one](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.com/click/e6065792/VaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucmVhbGNsZWFyaGVhbHRoLmNvbS9hcnRpY2xlcy8yMDI1LzEyLzA4L2hvd19hbWVyaWNhX2Nhbl9kZWZ1c2VfdGhlX2FsemhlaW1lcnNfZWNvbm9taWNfYm9tYl8xMTUxOTM1Lmh0bWw/SZW1haWxfZnJlZXRoaW5rZXJkYWlseV9jb20yNjAyMTc/LbmNsTjdEdUtBVw/gaZTcIg/s4meb7276cc)**. Without a serious strategy, the growing number of Alzheimer’s cases could strain families, shrink the workforce, and place additional pressure on federal programs.
**China has a plan. Where’s America’s Plan?**
China has launched a national Alzheimer’s effort focused on awareness, screening, and early intervention. America needs a similar focus. The health and wellness of our citizens and the fiscal strength of our nation are at stake.
The encouraging news is that the path forward is becoming clearer. It must include:
* Detecting the disease earlier
* Empowering primary care doctors
* Supporting innovation
* Reducing bureaucratic obstacles
* Putting patients back at the center of care

With the right strategy, America can lead the world by extending not just lifespan, but healthspan, allowing millions to remain active contributors to their families, communities, and economies.
Dr. Beasley reminds us that behind every policy debate is a human story and hope is no longer theoretical. Now the question is whether we will learn from stories like his and act boldly to help families facing an Alzheimer’s diagnosis.

* * *

**About the Author:**
_Charles Sauer is the president of the Market Institute, and the author of Profit Motive: What Drives the Things We Do._

About Marlene Galan-Woods
Marlene Galán-Woods is a former broadcast journalist and mother of five who has lived in Arizona for the past 36 years. Her parents fled communist Cuba looking for a better life. February 17. 2026
Although I am a conservative Republican, I always had a grudging admiration for Jesse Jackson. And not because he was civil rights advocate. Civil rights advocates are a dime a dozen.
But Rev. Jackson was basically a street fighter who fought the system, especially the compliant Black civil rights establishment and the Democrat Party insiders who rigged their Convention rules to deny him the voice he deserved during his highly successful runs for President.
Jackson was born in the Jim Crow South in 1941, to an 18-year-old high school student who was impregnated by her 33-year-old married neighbor. Perhaps that was why he was [strongly pro-life ](https://substack.com/redirect/f7d88195-60e5-4b06-bfe8-57ed65f318ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)until his Presidential ambitions forced him to flip-flop. He excelled academically but many do not realize he was also an accomplished athlete, lettering in baseball, basketball and football in high school and playing quarterback for North Carolina A&T. A natural leader, he was also a high school and college class president.
He became a Baptist Minister and an acolyte of the rising civil rights leader, Martin Luther King. With Reverend King's assassination, Jackson and the Rev. Ralph Abernathy had a brutal political fight over several years as to who would continue King's legacy. But Jackson's charisma and superior organizational ability prevailed and by the late 1970s, Jackson was seen by the media and general population as the spokesman for Blacks.

He parlayed this visibility into a run for President in 1984. He set fire to his potential campaign by becoming the first Black to address the Alabama legislature and stated: "It is about time we forgot about black and white and started talking about employed and unemployed".
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcdb736d-2b80-466c-8d9d-499416490709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Rev. Jackson with fighter pilot Lt. Goodman after negotiating his release.

His populist message resonated, and he won the early primaries of New Hampshire and South Carolina. But Democratic party insiders, believing he was unelectable, [manipulated the delegate rules](https://substack.com/redirect/ac87dced-aece-4447-a40e-cba5daa1b464?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) so that Jackson soon fell too far behind in the delegate count destroying his momentum. This enabled Walter Mondale to win later primaries, gather the most votes and become the nominee. Mondale went on to lose 49 of the 50 states. No one knows if Jackson would have done better, but it is unlikely he could have done worse.
Jackson again sought the Democratic nomination in 1988, with similar results.
Jackson was not without his faults. He once referred to New York City as "Hymietown" although he later apologized for such blatant antisemitism. He delivered a commencement address at Medgar Evers College in which he stated that young people were "experiencing an ethical collapse, a spiritual withdrawal, and escaping this reality through drugs, alcohol, sex without love, making unwanted babies and turning on each other with violence." Yet he cheated on his wife, fathering a child out of wedlock. And he defended the [huckster Jessie Smollett,](https://substack.com/redirect/bd671357-1dc2-4479-bfb3-15a6f6b5388f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) even after it was obvious that Smollett staged the attack against him by supposed Trump supporters.

Jackson had the ability to build bridges with those on the opposite side of the fence. He met with segregationist Alabama Governor George Wallace and stated afterwards "[Wallace is] one of the most forward of any governor across the South in terms of the sharing of appointments with blacks and whites and women, and the tone of the administration had changed".
He was an occasional guest on conservative icon William Buckley's Firing Line and could his own to [Buckley's incisive questions](https://substack.com/redirect/a2ef8391-e027-4e54-8001-e388d8d38362?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The two men became such friends that when Buckley was hospitalized, Jackson came to visit and the two men prayed together.
When fighter pilot Lt Robert O. Goodman was shot down over Lebanon in 1984, Jackson irritated the diplomatic establishment and led a delegation that [negotiated his release](https://substack.com/redirect/3e6c5d93-ca05-43d4-8966-b6a7995423ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Upon returning to the United States, President Reagan had the two men come to the White House and commented on Jackson's diplomacy with the statement: "You can't argue with success."

According to published reports, Rev. Jackson died of [PSP or Progressive Supranuclear Palsy.](https://substack.com/redirect/201104ab-384b-4c47-ad44-065656a59d99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) But none of these articles mentioned what a hideous disease this is. PSP is a neurological disease similar to Parkinson's that results in balance loss, poor eye movement and behavioral changes. But its most devastating symptom is inability to swallow, resulting in episodes of choking and aspiration pneumonia. It is possible that Rev. Jackson's last months were extremely unpleasant, to put in mildly.

But Jackson will be remembered as a true American who successfully went to bat for those he believed were oppressed. And he lifted the lives of many. As President Reagan said, "You can't argue with success."

And not because he was civil rights advocate. Civil rights advocates are a dime a dozen. But Rev. Jackson was basically a street fighter who fought the system, especially the compliant Black civil rights establishment and the Democrat Party insiders who rigged their Convention rules to deny him the voice he deserved during his highly successful runs for President. Jackson was born in the Jim Crow South in 1941, to an 18-year-old high school student who was impregnated by her 33-year-old married neighbor. Perhaps that was why he was his Presidential ambitions forced him to flip-flop. He excelled academically but many do not realize he was also an accomplished athlete, lettering in baseball, basketball and football in high school and playing quarterback for North Carolina A&T. A natural leader, he was also a high school and college class president. He became a Baptist Minister and an acolyte of the rising civil rights leader, Martin Luther King. With Reverend King's assassination, Jackson and the Rev. Ralph Abernathy had a brutal political fight over several years as to who would continue King's legacy. But Jackson's charisma and superior organizational ability prevailed and by the late 1970s, Jackson was seen by the media and general population as the spokesman for Blacks. He parlayed this visibility into a run for President in 1984. He set fire to his potential campaign by becoming the first Black to address the Alabama legislature and stated: "It is about time we forgot about black and white and started talking about employed and unemployed". | | ---|---|--- Rev. Jackson with fighter pilot Lt. Goodman after negotiating his release. His populist message resonated, and he won the early primaries of New Hampshire and South Carolina. But Democratic party insiders, believing he was unelectable, so that Jackson soon fell too far behind in the delegate count destroying his momentum. This enabled Walter Mondale to win later primaries, gather the most votes and become the nominee. Mondale went on to lose 49 of the 50 states. No one knows if Jackson would have done better, but it is unlikely he could have done worse. Jackson again sought the Democratic nomination in 1988, with similar results. Jackson was not without his faults. He once referred to New York City as "Hymietown" although he later apologized for such blatant antisemitism. He delivered a commencement address at Medgar Evers College in which he stated that young people were "experiencing an ethical collapse, a spiritual withdrawal, and escaping this reality through drugs, alcohol, sex without love, making unwanted babies and turning on each other with violence." Yet he cheated on his wife, fathering a child out of wedlock. And he defended the even after it was obvious that Smollett staged the attack against him by supposed Trump supporters. Jackson had the ability to build bridges with those on the opposite side of the fence. He met with segregationist Alabama Governor George Wallace and stated afterwards "[Wallace is] one of the most forward of any governor across the South in terms of the sharing of appointments with blacks and whites and women, and the tone of the administration had changed". He was an occasional guest on conservative icon William Buckley's Firing Line and could his own to . The two men became such friends that when Buckley was hospitalized, Jackson came to visit and the two men prayed together. When fighter pilot Lt Robert O. Goodman was shot down over Lebanon in 1984, Jackson irritated the diplomatic establishment and led a delegation that . Upon returning to the United States, President Reagan had the two men come to the White House and commented on Jackson's diplomacy with the statement: "You can't argue with success." According to published reports, Rev. Jackson died of But none of these articles mentioned what a hideous disease this is. PSP is a neurological disease similar to Parkinson's that results in balance loss, poor eye movement and behavioral changes. But its most devastating symptom is inability to swallow, resulting in episodes of choking and aspiration pneumonia. It is possible that Rev. Jackson's last months were extremely unpleasant, to put in mildly. But Jackson will be remembered as a true American who successfully went to bat for those he believed were oppressed. And he lifted the lives of many. As President Reagan said, "You can't argue with success." For the past few weeks, I've been on the streets, in downtown Salt Lake City, on Main Street in Park City during Sundance, at UVU and outside BYU.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/017c1d24-c90b-47c1-a204-e741b0663325?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
After the murders of Renee Good and Alex Pretti sparked protests across the country, I couldn't shake a feeling I didn't quite know how to name. Watching the videos online, it felt close. I kept imagining what it would mean to step between someone vulnerable and harm and not come home.
Helping people shouldn't cost you your life.
I feel much less safe in America than I did a year ago. Not because of immigrants but because armed federal agents have shot and killed people during enforcement operations, and the government's response was lies rather than truth. That unsettles me. So I showed up.
Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..O9VkZxML5zUR0eSmoeAdSX8gkvbnNiiYL9J-kSM1yqY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=188312040)
I stood outside during this abnormally warm winter alongside students, parents, veterans, alumni, neighbors, people trying to understand what "security" now means in America. I kept circling back to that word: Security.
One afternoon at a protest against ICE recruitment at BYU, a mom stood with her child on her shoulders, neon signs glowing in the sun. She asked her daughter, "Who does Jesus love?" The little girl answered without hesitation: "Everyone."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9754c67f-1531-441b-aa11-2ebc1ca345fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The crowd roared. That child knew what adults sometimes forget; her answer was instinctive. It was what belonging sounds like before we complicate it.
At UVU, students held a sit-in during another ICE recruitment event on campus. Since the shooting of Charlie Kirk earlier this year on that same campus, tensions have been high. I was admittedly nervous to enter. But what I remember wasn't confrontation, it was a movement powered by love.
Students walked the halls singing:
"It's okay to change your mind.
Show us your courage, leave this behind.
It's okay to change your mind.
You can join us here anytime."
It wasn't angry or shaming. Despite the trauma many students carry from witnessing a murder firsthand, they showed up with moral courage and invited others to join. That lyric has stayed with me.
On a warm winter afternoon outside the City and County Building in downtown Salt Lake City, speaker Samantha Reagan's questions echoed:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0f9f7154-d022-4840-948c-87bcfddc441a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"Did your undocumented neighbor raise your rent?
Did your undocumented neighbor cut your wages?
Did your undocumented neighbor lay you off?
Did your undocumented neighbor raise your grocery prices?
Did your undocumented neighbor deny you healthcare?
Undocumented or documented, my neighbor is still my neighbor, and they have more in common with me than any billionaire does."
Security isn't just about who crosses a border. It's about who shapes the system.
When I think about what the Department of Homeland Security should mean, I don't picture masked ICE agents on the streets, recruitment tables at universities or Kristi Noem flying in a private jet. I think about what makes people feel secure. A roof overhead. Heat in winter and cool in summer. Food on the table. Access to healthcare. Clean air and water.
Knowing that if disaster strikes, someone shows up.
I think about immigrants who build our houses, run our favorite restaurants, and train at the Utah Olympic Oval. I think about athletes like Shruti Kotwal, chasing Olympic dreams on the fastest ice in the world, yet forced to navigate a broken visa system and legal uncertainty just to stay and compete. I think about scientists, students, and entrepreneurs deciding whether this country feels stable enough to build a life in. They are the people making our communities better.
Right now, the government is shutdown over immigration funding. This makes our questions even **more** important. Trump tells us that immigrants are the root of economic instability, but that instability is actually driven by concentrated wealth and policy decisions that his own administration's policies only intensify.
He points the finger at the vulnerable so we don't notice how he and his allies are profiting from the chaos.
If security means anything, it should mean clarity and fairness.
More immigration judges to clear backlogs.
Modernized visa processing.
Realistic legal pathways aligned with workforce needs.
Transparent oversight.
That's what real governance looks like. Maybe the bravest thing we can do right now is ask ourselves what security actually feels like, and who it includes.
"It's okay to change your mind."
I'm still thinking about that.
If this piece resonated with you, I'm asking you to do two things today to help us build a more secure and transparent community:
1. **Keep Shruti on the Ice:** Shruti Kotwal is India's fastest woman on ice, and she trains right here at the Utah Olympic Oval. Her O-1 athlete visa expires this June. We are raising funds to cover her immediate legal and immigration filing fees so that a visa deadline doesn't end her Olympic dream.
👉 [help keep Shruti on the ice](https://substack.com/redirect/7a6b552e-7802-4324-bf7f-1786ed523e3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
2. **Demand Accountability from Senator John Curtis:** It's hard to trust our leaders to fix a broken immigration system when they are profiting from it. Senator Curtis holds a financial interest in Action Target, a Utah company that makes millions from DHS and ICE contracts. Join me in asking him to divest from these interests or recuse himself from votes that affect his own bottom line.
👉 **[sign the petition here](https://substack.com/redirect/f1de94d0-18c1-424b-a49e-b76dd3ed90b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Friend,
You know I’m not shy about calling out Donald Trump. But when it comes to this administration’s extreme agenda, there’s another name that deserves just as much blame: JD Vance.
Vance is as loyal a Trump lapdog as you’ll find. He pushed through Trump’s reckless tariffs. He gutted health care to fund a tax cut for billionaires. He unleashed evil and violence in our communities – resulting in American citizens being gunned down on residential streets.
**The spiritual rot in this White House is worse than you could ever imagine, and JD Vance doesn’t think he’ll ever have to pay a political price for it.**
Today, I’m asking you to help prove him wrong. To show him that the American people are rightfully outraged, and that we’re not going to forget that he’s to blame for what’s happening in our country.
**My team created a new poll so you can make it clear where you stand, and I’m counting on your response by midnight tonight. Please, speak out now:**
**Do you approve of JD Vance as Vice President?**

[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi, I wanted to make sure you saw this news.

For months, Donald Trump’s Justice Department has been trying to get their
hands on Michigan’s voter registration lists – a blatant overreach and
violation of our citizens’ privacy.

We fought back – and last week a federal judge once again blocked Trump’s
abuse of power and protected Michigan’s voter data.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/2252?t=1001&akid=1528%2E181023%2EjEX9BA ][IMG]

This ruling is a victory for the people of Michigan and for the rule of
law. And let me be clear: our citizens’ private data is not up for grabs.

I will always stand up to anyone — no matter how powerful — to protect
Michiganders’ privacy and their rights. And I’m calling on state officials
across the country to stand firm and do the same.

We know this won’t be the end of the fight. You can bet the Trump
administration will keep doing whatever it can to get our voters’ personal
information – but I will fight back at every turn.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/2252?t=1002&akid=1528%2E181023%2EjEX9BA ]I’m running for Governor to protect the voices, votes, and economic
prosperity of every single person who calls Michigan home, and I hope
you’ll join me in this fight. Chip in $5 or whatever you can today to
protect Michigan from Trump’s continued abuses of power:

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/2252?t=1003&akid=1528%2E181023%2EjEX9BA ]Donate →

Thanks,

Jocelyn

body:
These Democrats voted to thank ICE.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260217-1&t=1&akid=3158%2E587540%2EIXtq4I)
Hi Peter,
Last summer, Democratic Reps. Shri Thanedar, Steve Cohen, and Stephen Lynch all voted for a resolution in Congress to “express gratitude” for ICE. While they were voting to thank ICE, Trump was actively deploying the US military to Los Angeles to crush peaceful anti-ICE protests. These are our Democratic lawmakers in action!
That’s why Leaders We Deserve is proud to support Democratic primary challengers in each of these districts and usher in a new wave of Democrats who don’t fold when it matters most. We can’t keep electing Democrats who are _this_ out of touch. We need young bold leaders like **Donavan McKinney, Justin J. Pearson,** and **Patrick Roath** who are the best of what the next generation has to offer — not more of the status quo.
ICE is terrorizing our communities. And we need Democrats who are actively fighting back.
That's why this cycle we’re challenging Democrats who have truly failed to meet this moment and are in safe congressional seats that in no way risk us losing the House. Our party cannot be seen as complicit in the invasion of our communities by masked federal agents who are there purely to terrorize communities and be Trump's paramilitary force. Our party cannot just stand by and applaud communities standing up to ICE while the Democratic Members of Congress with the real power to make change do little to nothing to stop ICE and even make it a priority to thank ICE.
If you are tired of having a party that says it can’t do anything because it’s in the minority and then miraculously still claims it can't do anything because of Republicans even when we have all three branches of government, now is the time to join us in this movement and build a party that actually fights back.
**[Peter, make a $5 contribution now to support Leaders We Deserve. We deserve better Democrats — so we’re electing them.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260217_1_ice.s51R6A&refcode=em20260217-3158&amount=5&t=2&akid=3158%2E587540%2EIXtq4I)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

body:
The lies and attacks on vote-by-mail have only increased from MAGA, Team. Trump's statement has brought all the usual anti-voting, anti-democracy suspects out of the woodwork to ramp up the falsehoods we've heard for years.
But we've also seen defenders of voting rights standing up for our fundamental right to vote. We've just got to make sure our grassroots power can match their dark money millions and suppressive media empire.
RUSH $35 or more right now to fuel our work in the states, in Congress, and in the courts to defend mail-in voting and make every vote count in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021726_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
ABC: Trump says he will lead 'movement' to end mail-in voting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021726_2&amount=25]
Be prepared to hear about this all the way through the midterms, Team .
President Donald Trump has said that he is leading a "movement" to get rid of mail-in ballots and voting machines , falsely claiming that they lead to voter fraud.
Word for lying word: " I am going to lead a movement to get rid of MAIL-IN BALLOTS, and also, while we're at it, Highly 'Inaccurate,' Very Expensive, and Seriously Controversial VOTING MACHINES, which cost Ten Times more than accurate and sophisticated Watermark Paper, which is faster, and leaves NO DOUBT, at the end of the evening, as to who WON, and who LOST, the Election. "
How is Trump going to do this? He's signing an executive order ahead of next year's critical midterms. Is this just another attempt to distract from a failing economy, rising prices, and his role in the Epstein scandal? Probably, yes. Are we going to fight him tooth and nail? You betcha.
We're going to work in the states to defend our access to cast ballots, as they run elections. We're going to petition members of Congress to stop harmful bills that might attempt to back up this executive order. And we're going to do everything we can to support the efforts to stop this in court.
We'll be blunt: We still need your help to protect our fundamental right to vote. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to defend vote by mail across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021726_2&amount=35]

Trump has long lied about mail-in voting. He's claimed mail-in voting contributed to his 2020 election loss, though no widespread fraud has been found. In fact, the one case of mail-in ballot fraud in Pennsylvania after the 2020 election was a man who was prosecuted for returning his dead mother's ballot for Trump .
We all know just how safe and secure mail-in voting is. It's use dates back to the Civil War. The use of mail-in voting has become very common across the country and study after study has shown that fraud in mail-ballot voting is rare. There are also several safeguards in place nationwide to protect against fraud, including signature requirements and barcodes to track envelopes sent by officials. States have spent tens of millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing.
Being blunt: There is no good-faith reason to limit vote-by-mail access. There is no good-faith reason to end the use of mail-in voting, or do the other things in this forthcoming executive order or his previous one attacking vote-by-mail. Just like the wave of redistricting efforts in Texas, Florida, and beyond -- this is a partisan voter suppression exercise meant to codify MAGA's power in perpetuity and end our democracy.

subject: How to make sure your ballot is counted under the new rule >>
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260217-processing-pet [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260217-processing-pet]
I want to flag something important — and honestly, a little alarming.
A new U.S. Postal Service rule that went into effect on Christmas Eve quietly changed how postmarks are defined. That might sound technical, but stick with me — it has real consequences for everyday people, including whether your ballot counts and whether time-sensitive documents like tax returns are considered on time.
Here’s the change: A postmark used to generally reflect the day you dropped your mail off. Now, it officially reflects the day your mail is processed — which could be days later, depending on how far your local post office is from a regional processing center.
Why does that matter?
In states where mail-in ballots must be postmarked by Election Day, this change could mean the difference between your vote being counted or rejected — even if you did everything right.
As the Postal Service consolidates processing facilities, many post offices are now 50 to 150 miles away from where mail is actually postmarked. That distance creates delays that voters can’t control.
This isn’t just about elections. It affects tax filings, legal documents, and any deadline-driven mail that relies on a postmark.
There are ways to protect yourself:
* Bring time-sensitive mail to a staffed post office counter and request a free manual postmark
* Mail important items earlier than you think you need to
* For taxes, confirm whether private carriers are allowed for your filing
* Always check your state and local election rules
I’m sharing this because democracy doesn’t fail all at once — it erodes quietly, through technical changes most people never hear about until it’s too late.
I’m fighting to make sure voters are protected, informed, and never silenced by bureaucracy. If you believe people shouldn’t lose their vote to a processing delay, please add your name to my petition to say you believe voters have the right to be heard. ---|---|---
_**"[When a government has ceased to protect the lives, liberty, and property of the people ... and ... becomes an instrument in the hands of evil rulers for their oppression ... it is a ... sacred obligation to their posterity to abolish such government, and create another in its stead.](https://substack.com/redirect/cb60d8f9-0e74-4cb5-91a5-e702321b23cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
[Sam Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/96950bb4-1543-49b6-bd67-f9a94ab6bbbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
A growing confrontation is emerging between President Trump's aggressive immigration enforcement and economic realities in Texas, where home builders are warning Republican lawmakers that continued raids on construction sites could permanently damage the party's prospects in the region while creating severe labor shortages in one of America's most critical housing markets.

Mario Guerrero, CEO of the South Texas Builders Association and a self-identified Trump voter, delivered a stark message during meetings with federal officials in early February: "South Texas will never be red again." Guerrero's comments highlight the mounting frustration within the construction industry, which relies heavily on immigrant labor to meet the state's robust housing demands.

The problem extends far beyond Texas. According to industry representatives, over 40% of construction workers in Texas are immigrants, with substantial percentages being undocumented. Recent immigration enforcement actions have created widespread labor shortages, delayed construction projects, and increased costs across the state. In 2025 alone, Texas would have constructed approximately 400,000 fewer homes without immigrant labor, contributing to the state's ongoing housing affordability crisis.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7d2dabdf-a66f-4b2a-916f-03ce504f3cf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
These issues have tangible economic consequences. Construction delays mean fewer homes on the market at a time when Texas faces significant housing shortages, driving up prices and potentially pricing out middle-class families. The decreased construction activity also threatens job growth in related industries, including materials suppliers, furniture manufacturers, and home goods retailers.

**"[Texas will again lift it's head and stand among the nations. It ought to do so, for no country upon the globe can compare with it in natural advantages.](https://substack.com/redirect/536c053b-0005-401a-9913-d5fe751d903c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"**
**[Sam Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/96950bb4-1543-49b6-bd67-f9a94ab6bbbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The political implications of these enforcement actions are profound for Republicans in Texas. South Texas has been an increasingly competitive region, with GOP candidates making significant inroads with Latino voters in recent election cycles. These demographic shifts have been driven by changing attitudes toward economic policy, cultural issues, and security concerns--gains that construction industry leaders warn are being jeopardized by aggressive immigration enforcement.

"For many Latino voters, immigration enforcement is deeply personal," notes a Republican strategist from Texas. "When family members or community members are affected by workplace raids, it doesn't just impact one person--it ripples through entire communities. Families with mixed immigration status are particularly vulnerable, and the political backlash can be sustained and generational."

Construction industry leaders have held multiple meetings with both the White House and congressional representatives, seeking a more targeted approach to immigration enforcement that focuses on criminal elements rather than disrupting law-abiding workers at construction sites. Their visits to Washington in early February underscore the industry's growing desperation.

In response to these concerns, Texas lawmakers from both parties are pursuing legislation that would create a new visa category specifically for construction workers. Representatives Monica De La Cruz (R-TX) and Lloyd Smucker (R-PA) have introduced the Essential Workers for Economic Advancement Act, which would establish an H-2C visa program modeled after existing agricultural worker visas.

The bipartisan effort reflects the political sensitivity of the issue in Texas, where both parties recognize the economic and electoral implications of construction labor shortages. The proposed bill would create a legal pathway for seasonal construction workers to address what builders describe as critical labor shortages, particularly in regions like South Texas where immigration enforcement has been most intense.

"We have to face reality - 40% of construction workers in Texas are immigrants," stated Representative Vicente Gonzalez (D-TX) in a social media post. "We need a legal framework that recognizes our economic needs while maintaining security priorities."

The response from Texas elected officials has been varied and, in some cases, politically complicated. Governor Greg Abbott, who has positioned himself as a strong advocate for border security, has largely maintained his support for aggressive immigration enforcement while simultaneously promoting economic growth across Texas.

Representative Henry Cuellar (D-TX), who recently received a pardon from Trump for accepting bribes and had hinted at switching parties, has been more vocal in advocating for the construction industry's concerns. Cuellar facilitated meetings between the South Texas Builders Association and congressional leaders in Washington.

Meanwhile, Representative Tony Gonzales (R-TX), who represents a border district, has introduced legislation aimed at enhancing border security while also working to address legitimate labor needs. His Homeland Threat Response Act focuses on closing legal gaps for Customs and Border Protection personnel but doesn't directly address the construction industry's visa concerns.

Other Texas Republicans have been notably quiet on the issue, likely reflecting the political tightrope they must walk between their party's base that demands stricter immigration enforcement and business constituents who rely on immigrant labor.
"[Texas is the finest portion of the globe that has ever blessed my vision!](https://substack.com/redirect/8a0be515-6154-4b9a-a2cb-ad74fabdf33f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
**[Sam Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/96950bb4-1543-49b6-bd67-f9a94ab6bbbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The immigration debate exposes a fundamental hypocrisy within Republican circles. While publicly advocating for strict immigration enforcement and deportations to appeal to their base, many Republican business interests depend heavily on cheap immigrant labor. This tension has only intensified under Trump's aggressive policies.

"We've always seen this necessary hypocrisy in American immigration policy," notes political analyst Maria Torres. "Republicans will never deprive American businesses of their cheap, exploitable labor. That would be un-American from an economic perspective, even as they decry illegal immigration politically."

This dynamic is particularly evident in Texas, where industries from construction to agriculture rely on immigrant labor, yet Republican politicians maintain tough-on-immigration rhetoric to satisfy their voter base. The result is a policy landscape that simultaneously enforcement-heavy and dependent on undocumented workers.

"[All new states are invested, more or less, by a class of noisy, second-rate men who are always in favor of rash and extreme measures, but Texas was absolutely overrun by such men.](https://substack.com/redirect/39b9bbf3-0fec-4f25-b2b1-b9b9b103b23f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
**[Sam Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/96950bb4-1543-49b6-bd67-f9a94ab6bbbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Nowhere is this contradiction more apparent than in Governor Greg Abbott's response to the controversial Colony Ridge development in Liberty County, often described as the "biggest trailer park in the United States" with an estimated property value of $1 million. The massive development, located northeast of Houston, has become a flashpoint in the immigration debate, serving as a haven for immigrant families while simultaneously drawing scrutiny over alleged cartel activity and inadequate infrastructure.

Despite his hardline stance on border security, Abbott has been criticized for what critics characterize as inaction regarding Colony Ridge. The governor's administration recently settled with developers for $68 million over alleged environmental and zoning violations, yet the development continues to expand rapidly, drawing numerous immigrant residents, many of whom are undocumented.

ICE conducted a major operation at Colony Ridge in February 2025, resulting in over 118 arrests and highlighting law enforcement concerns about criminal elements in the community. Critics argue that such developments, which provide affordable housing options for immigrant workers, effectively create sanctuaries that attract illegal immigration while allowing businesses to maintain a supply of cheap labor without providing adequate infrastructure or legal oversight.

This developing situation in Texas reflects broader tensions within the Republican coalition nationwide. The GOP's traditional support for business-friendly policies and free markets often conflicts with the increasingly hawkish immigration stance demanded by the party's base. The construction industry's warnings highlight how practical economic concerns can clash with ideological purity, particularly in states with significant immigrant populations.

The outcome of this debate could have far-reaching implications for the 2026 midterm elections, especially in Texas where competitive races are becoming increasingly common. If South Texas, once considered Democratic territory, shifts permanently back to the blue column due to immigration enforcement policies, it could effectively end Republican hopes of expanding their electoral map in the region.

"[Let me tell you what is coming. After the sacrifice of countless millions of treasure and hundreds of thousands of lives you may win Southern independence, but I doubt it. The North is determined to preserve this Union. They are not a fiery, impulsive people as you are, for they live in colder climates. But when they begin to move in a given direction, they move with the steady momentum and perseverance of a mighty avalanche.](https://substack.com/redirect/0022bb05-d66b-4740-bdb2-39cb701be285?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
**[Sam Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/96950bb4-1543-49b6-bd67-f9a94ab6bbbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Governor Greg Abbott has received significant political contributions from developers connected to the controversial Colony Ridge development in Liberty County. Campaign finance records show that the Texas development company responsible for Colony Ridge, along with its principals and affiliated entities, have donated over $750,000 to Abbott's gubernatorial campaigns since 2014. These donations came despite the development's controversial status as an unincorporated settlement that has drawn criticism for inadequate infrastructure and rapid expansion without proper zoning oversight.
What makes these contributions particularly noteworthy is their timing relative to regulatory actions against Colony Ridge. Donations surged during periods when the Texas Attorney General's office was investigating environmental violations and other infractions at the development, with Abbott's administration ultimately settling with the developers for $68 million in early 2026. Critics suggest these political connections may explain why enforcement actions were relatively lenient compared to other similar cases. Despite Abbott's hardline rhetoric on illegal immigration, the substantial contributions from developers who profit from housing immigrant communities highlight a disconnect between his stated positions and the financial relationships that may influence policy decisions.
The Colony Ridge donations exemplify the broader tension in Texas politics between tough-on-immigration rhetoric and the economic realities of Republican business supporters who benefit from immigrant labor and housing needs.

"[I would give no thought of what the world might say of me, if I could only transmit to posterity the reputation of an honest man.](https://substack.com/redirect/b5742bbb-0b17-4cf8-ba38-34002264f014?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
**[Sam Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/96950bb4-1543-49b6-bd67-f9a94ab6bbbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick thanked AG Paxton**** in a social media post and claimed credit for being "the first elected official to conduct an in-depth tour of **Colony** **Ridge** with law enforcement." Candidate for Governor Paxton announced a $68 million settlement with the developers of Colony Ridge, addressing allegations of deceptive lending and marketing practices targeting Latino homebuyers.
As the tension between immigration enforcement and economic needs continues to grow, several potential solutions are emerging. The bipartisan H-2C visa proposal represents one approach, but significant hurdles remain in Congress. Meanwhile, some states are exploring their own solutions to address labor shortages while maintaining security priorities.

For Texas builders, the immediate future remains uncertain. Construction projects continue to face delays and cost increases, while the political landscape shifts in unpredictable ways. What remains clear is that the intersection of immigration policy, economic needs, and electoral politics will continue to be a defining issue in Texas and potentially the nation for the foreseeable future.

"This isn't just about construction--it's about whether our communities can grow and thrive," Guerrero told lawmakers during his Washington visit. "When we can't build homes, when we can't expand businesses, when families are torn apart by enforcement actions, we all pay the price. That's a reality that transcends party lines and requires thoughtful solutions rather than blunt instruments."

"[I would lay down my life to defend any one of the States from aggression, which endangered peace or threatened its institutions. I could do more for the union, but I wish to do more; for the destruction of the union would be the destruction of all the States. A stab in the heart is worse then a cut in a limb, for this may be healed.](https://substack.com/redirect/e5fc8001-bc4f-45fa-bf74-e9f3b62df548?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
