name: Ashley Moody
subject: They’re saying “it’s just a special election.” Big mistake.
body:
| | | | Patriot,
A lot of Republicans are shrugging off the recent news out of Texas, where _**a deep red seat just swung an astonishing 32 points and a Democrat EASILY defeated the GOP candidate.**__**
**_They’re saying, _“Relax – it was just a special election.”_
**That should worry you - because the Senate majority may well hinge on a special election.****

| | During Black History Month, and all year long, we’re honored to celebrate the rich culture, resilience, and impact of Black Americans. And we recognize a proud legacy of pushing our nation towards its democratic ideals by commemorating the freedom fighters who organized, marched, bled, and died for the sacred right to vote. **One of those heroes was John Lewis.** Before serving as a Congressman, he was a major force in the Civil Rights Movement as a Freedom Rider, chairman of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, and a leader of the march across the Edmund Pettus Bridge on Bloody Sunday, which helped pave the way for the Voting Rights Act of 1965. His legacy endures as we continue to make good trouble in his honor and fight for his vision of a more just democracy. That’s because we know that his mission isn’t just a part of history. It’s still necessary in the present. And what we do today will shape the future of our democracy — and the survival of free and fair elections in America. This year, the Voting Rights Act could once again be gutted by the Supreme Court, which could pave the way for a new wave of racially discriminatory redistricting that slashes representation for Black Americans — eliminating up to 30% of the current seats held by members of the Congressional Black Caucus. The SAVE Act — a modern-day poll tax — could disenfranchise tens of millions of Americans, particularly impacting communities of color, if it’s passed through the Senate. And around the country, anti-voter extremists continue to try to restrict access to the ballot box in order to avoid true accountability from an electorate that is as diverse as America. We will keep on fighting back to support equal access to the ballot box. And your support helps combat the suppression and centuries-long silencing of Black voters in the United States as we work to ensure every voter’s voice is heard. Together, we’ll continue mobilizing for fair maps that ensure fair representation for all voters, rallying Americans in key states to contact their swing-vote Senators and urge them to reject the SAVE Act, and organizing for voting rights protections to thwart attempts at voter suppression. It’s how we honor Black history. And it’s how we ensure a more just future. In solidarity, The Fair Fight Action Team

Dear Fellow American, A fifth-grade girl traveled with her Colorado school on a field trip across the country.

You can probably imagine how she must have felt in the days and weeks leading up to the trip. Excited to spend a few days with her friends. Eager to visit a new place. And, sure, a bit nervous--it's a big deal to stay overnight in a place you've never been before, especially as an 11-year-old.

**Now imagine how she felt when she found out --already hundreds of miles from home and in her hotel room for the night--_that she was supposed to share a bed with a boy._**

Shocked. Confused. Uncomfortable.

She slipped into the bathroom to call her mom, who was thankfully on the trip with her. Her mom thought she must have misunderstood. She couldn't fathom that the school assigned her daughter to room overnight with a boy.

But it wasn't a misunderstanding. It was _ school policy_.

The policy says that students on overnight trips will be assigned rooms based on their "gender identity," not on biology. And the school refuses to notify parents or students of the policy, or if a student of the opposite sex is assigned to the room.

That means a girl can be assigned to share a hotel room with a boy who identifies as a girl, without mom and dad's--or the student's--knowledge or say.

**How would you feel if this happened to your child or grandchild?**

It shouldn't have to be said--but this is just **WRONG.**

It's common sense that girls and boys deserve to have their own private spaces. And if that privacy could be infringed upon, parents need to know so that they can make informed decisions for their children.

Families across the country are being harmed by policies like these. That's why the Waileses, along with three other Colorado families, are pushing back in a lawsuit--for their kids and many others like them.

Hey folks,
**Katie Phang** and I jumped into this episode thinking we'd talk Colbert and the FCC--and ended up in a full-on, no-BS debate about primaries, party control, Trump voters, and what it actually takes to win a state like Texas. It was messy in the best way. Honest. A little uncomfortable. Exactly the kind of conversation we should be having.
**Here 's where it went:**
* [**00:01:07**] We kick off with Obama nostalgia, Netflix rabbit holes, and why it weirdly felt good to see Barack and Michelle back in the mix. Energy shift. You could feel it.
* [**00:04:09**] The Colbert-Tallarico showdown: CBS tries to block the interview, the FCC flexes, and Colbert basically says "nope" and runs it anyway. We break down why this censorship attempt completely backfired.
* [**00:09:54**] The Texas primary fight gets real. Tallarico vs. Crockett. Electability vs. authenticity. Who actually expands the map in a Trump +10 state?
* [**00:13:36**] Competitive primaries: Are they healthy or self-sabotage? We dig into the Democratic discomfort with messy contests--and why avoiding them might be costing us.
* [**00:24:02**] The hardest question of all: Do Democrats need to win back Trump voters? Or is that the wrong frame entirely? This is where it got raw. Strategy vs. values. Movement vs. persuasion.

This episode is for anyone who's tired of surface-level political takes. We talked about what it means to actually believe in a candidate. About being wrong. About listening. About the tension between wanting to win and wanting to stand for something. And yeah--we disagreed in places. That's the point. If you value conversations that don't dodge the hard stuff--if you believe we get stronger by wrestling with the strategy instead of pretending it's settled--help me keep building this space.

--Mike

Most don’t know this, but while I’m running for Congress, I’m also teaching students at my local community college. These aren’t your typical four-year college students. They’re moms. They’re immigrants. They’re folks holding down night shifts, raising families, but still showing up because they believe in building something better. **That’s the story of the Central Valley. It was my family’s story -- and it’s the story my opponent David Valadao has turned his back on.** He’s voting for the interests of billionaires and the far-right -- not the working people I see every day. Friend, I grew up in a military family, so we moved around a lot. But no matter where we lived, we were always outdoors, running through the desert with my cousins, fishing with my dad, or walking the cornfields with my grandfather. Back then, I never imagined that those moments would shape my path, **[let alone lead me to run for governor of New Mexico.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=3&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=4&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)
From my great-grandmother, mother, and many before them, I’m blessed to come from generations of Pueblo women who taught me what it means to be fierce and resilient — and I’ve carried these values with me my entire life.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=5&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)
My parents didn’t graduate from college, but they believed deeply in giving back and helping others. They taught me that where you come from matters, and that service is about showing up for people. It’s why I tell kids not to forget their roots, and why I believe everyone, no matter their background, has something to offer their community.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=6&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)
I carried those values when I started working at my local bakery right after high school; when I volunteered at my child’s preschool to help reduce the cost of tuition; and when I started my own small business producing and canning homemade salsa.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=7&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)
I carried them with me when I was a single mom living paycheck to paycheck, relying on food stamps and WIC to help keep my child fed and healthy.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=8&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)
And I carried those values with me as one of the first Native American women elected to Congress and then as the first Native Secretary of the Interior.

**To this day, those values of ferocity and resilience _[fuel my fight to advocate for working families and deliver progress for all New Mexicans.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=9&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)_**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=10&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)
But here’s the thing: **The governor’s seat has a history of switching parties every eight years, and GOP donors are already preparing to spend millions to defeat me. If we're going to buck the trend, I need you on my grassroots team, Friend.**
**_[So please, will you contribute $5 or more today to help me become our next governor and create a better future for all New Mexicans?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk383-fr-nd&amount=5&t=11&akid=7590%2E400544%2EOospY3)_**

I carried them with me when I was a single mom living paycheck to paycheck, relying on food stamps and WIC to help keep my child fed and healthy. And I carried those values with me as one of the first Native American women elected to Congress and then as the first Native Secretary of the Interior. To this day, those values of ferocity and resilience But here’s the thing: The governor’s seat has a history of switching parties every eight years, and GOP donors are already preparing to spend millions to defeat me. If we're going to buck the trend, I need you on my grassroots team, Friend. | | Be fierce, Deb | | | | |

Ramadan Mubarak,
Peter. 🌙 🤲🏽

For Muslims around the world, this is a month of reflection, discipline,
and generosity. A time to fast, to pray, and to give.

There’s a concept in our faith called Sadaqah — a kind of charity given
from the heart, focused on building something that lasts.

That’s what I’ve been thinking about in this moment.

The truth is, it shouldn’t be this hard in the richest country in the
world to afford healthcare, groceries, or housing. No one should have to
rely on charity or a GoFundMe to simply get by.

But our politics has been corrupted by corporations, billionaires, and
oligarchs who have monetized our pain for their profit.

I know we can build something better, and that’s the guiding spirit of our
campaign.

We’re one of the only campaigns in the country willing to stand up to both
Trumpism and the corporate corruption inside our own party. That means
powerful interests will spend heavily to stop us.

The only way we win is together,
Peter.

If you’re not in a place to give, I respect that deeply. Your support,

I’m grateful for you. Truly.

Wishing you a peaceful and purposeful Ramadan,

Abdul

name: Corey DeAngelis, Americans for Fair Treatment
subject: Teachers’ dues are funding activism they don’t support
body:
You won’t believe what union bosses are funding with teachers’ dues

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e16514177/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvOEZnQlI4VDRkdQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAyMTc/LbmNsYmdCU2E0WA/qP2hpZHM9bmM0WkxTN0VndVlXOGFscw/gaZT4jg/s7jd83e7e0c)
| |
---
| | Patriot,
---
Washington state is about to become ground zero in a fight for basic sanity. And the union bosses are panicking. They’re afraid because moms and dads gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures to put two simple ideas on the ballot: Parental rights. And fairness in girls’ sports. _That’s it._ Nothing extreme, nothing radical. Just common sense. **But instead of listening to their own members, teachers unions are spending workers’ dues to crush these ballot measures.** You read that right, Patriot. The SAME dues teachers are forced to pay... The SAME dues that are supposed to protect their rights... **Are now being used to fight against the values of most Americans.** _And probably many of their own members._ Americans for Fair Treatment is the leading organization fighting to empower public sector workers – like teachers – when their unions act in ways that violate their values. **[Will you join us in holding public sector unions accountable for ignoring the voice of their members with your gift of $25, $50, $100, or any amount you can give today?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ **Help Teachers Hold Their Unions Accountable** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Patriot, here’s what these initiatives would do: One restores parental rights, so moms and dads can see school records. So they can opt out of certain lessons. _So they are not kept in the dark about their own kids._ The other protects girls’ sports by requiring athletes to compete based on biological sex. So girls don’t lose scholarships, their safety, or fairness in their athletics. Simple. But the unions hate it, because this fight isn’t just about education anymore. **It’s about power.** They already dumped serious money into stopping these measures during the signature phase. They sent mailers... trained activists... pressured businesses... and attacked grassroots volunteers. **All funded by workers’ dues.** Dues paid by teachers who just want to teach. Dues paid by public employees who NEVER signed up for culture wars. **Patriot, that’s the real scandal.** Union leaders are taking money from hardworking Americans and using it to push politics their own members may not even support. Patriot, that’s why Americans for Fair Treatment exists. Not to scream or posture, but to guide public employees who feel trapped. Caught in unions that speak for them. Spend for them. _And embarrass them._ We show workers their rights. We help them opt out. We stand with them when unions retaliate. **Not only that, but we also expose how union bosses spend their money.** AFFT isn’t new to fights like these. We were built for this moment. Americans for Fair Treatment was founded to defend public employees from union abuse. From day one, our mission has been simple: Give workers the facts. Give them their rights. And give them a way out. And we’ve delivered real results. In just the past year alone... We helped free **50,000 TSA officers** from union control, the largest worker freedom victory in American history. We secured a major federal court victory that allows federal workers to sue unions directly. We’ve exposed corruption inside powerful government unions. And we’ve helped thousands of teachers, first responders, and public employees keep their hard-earned money. **These victories are only possible because donors like you stepped up, Patriot.** **[Can I count on you to step up today and chip in $25, $50, $100 or more to help us empower public sector employees and hold their unions accountable for ignoring their voice and their values?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ **Help Teachers Hold Their Unions Accountable** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Patriot, now the fight is moving to the ballot, unions will spend millions more to overturn the will of the people. body:
Why Virginia needs to act while others rig the system
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260217-185&t=1&akid=185%2E12592%2El8XlaG)
**What is happening right now should be a wake-up call for Virginians.**
Across the country, Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans have been aggressively pushing to redraw congressional maps in states like Texas and Florida — all to lock in power before voters ever cast a ballot. _These efforts aren’t about earning support. They’re about manipulating maps to tilt elections in their favor._
As _The Hill_ recently reported, we’re in a _“totally unique moment,”_ driven by coordinated national pressure to reshape representation before the next election.
**That national context matters here in Virginia.**
**When other states move forward with new congressional maps ahead of the midterms without voter approval, Virginians risk having our representation in Congress weakened if we do nothing. Virginians for Fair Elections exists to make sure voters here — not politicians — stay in control.**
The YES on fair elections amendment we’re fighting for is about fairness and transparency. It gives Virginians a temporary, voter-approved way to respond to this unprecedented moment, while preserving our bipartisan redistricting process after the 2030 census. Voters will see the proposed maps. Voters will have the final say.
But voters can’t protect what they don’t know about.
This isn’t about partisan games. It is about making sure Virginia doesn’t fall behind while others try to rig the system — and that Virginians’ voices in Washington remain strong and fairly represented.
[**If you can, please chip in today to help us educate voters across the Commonwealth and protect fair representation for Virginia.**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260217_2.SBqnKh&amount=3&refcode=20260217-185&t=2&akid=185%2E12592%2El8XlaG)

body:

# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260217-5925-footer&t=1&akid=5925%2E420207%2EDNGCUD)
Peter, this is outrageous:
**The Department of Justice is spying on members of Congress — including me — as we search the Epstein files to hold them accountable.**
[****](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/51821?c0=pj-em-20260217.PZB094&refcode=em20260217-5925&t=2&akid=5925%2E420207%2EDNGCUD)
Members of Congress should be able to conduct oversight without the Department of Justice spying on us.
Spying on my search history with a “burn book” of exactly what emails I searched is totally inappropriate. As a member of Congress, it’s imperative that I look for technical answers as to why exactly the DOJ thought it was okay to release the names of survivors while failing to investigate the predators that need to be brought to justice.
It is my job to hold them accountable, and it violates long-established democratic norms for the DOJ to surveil us as we conduct oversight. Seeing a burn book spying on my search history for the “un-redacted” Epstein files took this beyond the law.
**We can’t undo the failure of Pam Bondi’s Department of Justice. But we can decide what happens next.**

Happy Fastnacht Day!
For as long as I can remember, the day before Ash Wednesday, known to many as Fat Tuesday, has been for making fastnachts, a traditional Pennsylvania Dutch doughnut.
Every year, my family gets together at someone's house -- first my grandparents', then my mom's, now my aunt's -- and gets to work making dough, waiting for it to rise, rolling out and cutting up the doughnuts, and then frying them. We eat as many as we can, and then bag up the rest and take them around to neighbors.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d11ecb76-8839-49c3-9eb8-756eede77aca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You can eat them plain, shake them up in a bag of powdered sugar (my personal favorite), or have them with some molasses.
Fastnacht Day is one of the reasons why I love this part of Pennsylvania so much -- our traditions, our sense of community, our love of all things dough.
If you did not get a doughnut from a Wallace, a Fleagle, or a Shollenberger today, I'll have a few at the Berks County petition signing event tonight! And if that's not your neck of the woods, then find a way today to treat yourself and your neighbors.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d11ecb76-8839-49c3-9eb8-756eede77aca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

name: Chris Brooks, LCV
subject: A breath of fresh air
body:
“I just need a breath of fresh air.”

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM0ODc4MjUS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQwMDc4NjAzNgS2&mt=1&rt=0).
| | | |
---
| | |
* * *
---
| | “I just need a breath of fresh air.”
---
| | Last week, I was sitting across from one of my colleagues when she announced that she was going outside for a breath of fresh air before our next meeting. I didn’t think twice about the meaning of her comment until later, when we were talking about the implications of the Trump administration’s massive step backward on keeping the air we breathe clean and safe.
---
| | By now, you may have heard that Trump announced the repeal of the Endangerment Finding last week. This means that the EPA no longer has a responsibility to limit the air pollutants causing climate change, including those spewed out of cars and trucks, and that the air we all breathe is about to get much dirtier and more dangerous. It’s easy to miss earth-shattering news like this, when we’re fed disastrous headlines every day, but this is a big deal we should all be paying attention to. I encourage you to check out LCV’s very own Matthew Davis speaking about it on Good Morning America, or [**watch him break it down in this video**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/k_ypT7vzzDC7/VHdnTzhWakZKbjlXQ1IyOHVGZ1lqQVlDU1FOSTZkVDZBT3hIckMvUFBMWW9qYXBTSU5vSHA2WTY1M3dLaEI1SmJsV0NhV05ZN0FoMUw3WnRkQ1BKMGJ1NXFYaDlicnA5ZzJHTWRlVXZYTzQ9S0/).
---
| | My colleague’s ability to get a breath of fresh air between meetings is one of the most trivial impacts of this rollback. There will be more heart attacks, asthma attacks, and other serious health issues that will be felt hardest by the most vulnerable people among us.
---
| | Right now, I’m having a hard time getting my head around the fact that the very concept of fresh air might soon be relegated to nostalgia, along with my childhood memories of cassette tapes and Beanie Babies. I’m terrified that in the not so distant future, clean, fresh air could become something I remember fondly, but rarely have access to.
---
| | But I have hope, too. Working at LCV has shown me that change is always possible when enough people take action for our collective good. My colleagues are brilliant, dedicated, and work tirelessly to protect our democracy and planet. I know the LCV community — staff and members alike — won’t stop fighting for a safe, livable climate, clean water, and clean air — but we have hard work ahead of us.
---
| | I thank you for your support of this important work, and I encourage us all to step outside once in a while for a breath of fresh air... we can’t take this for granted.
---
| | Best,
---
| | Chris Brooks, VP of MembershipLCV
---

clean_body: “I just need a breath of fresh air.” If you are unable to see the message below, . | | | | | | | | | “I just need a breath of fresh air.” | | Last week, I was sitting across from one of my colleagues when she announced that she was going outside for a breath of fresh air before our next meeting. I didn’t think twice about the meaning of her comment until later, when we were talking about the implications of the Trump administration’s massive step backward on keeping the air we breathe clean and safe. | | By now, you may have heard that Trump announced the repeal of the Endangerment Finding last week. This means that the EPA no longer has a responsibility to limit the air pollutants causing climate change, including those spewed out of cars and trucks, and that the air we all breathe is about to get much dirtier and more dangerous. It’s easy to miss earth-shattering news like this, when we’re fed disastrous headlines every day, but this is a big deal we should all be paying attention to. I encourage you to check out LCV’s very own Matthew Davis speaking about it on Good Morning America, or . | | My colleague’s ability to get a breath of fresh air between meetings is one of the most trivial impacts of this rollback. There will be more heart attacks, asthma attacks, and other serious health issues that will be felt hardest by the most vulnerable people among us. | | Right now, I’m having a hard time getting my head around the fact that the very concept of fresh air might soon be relegated to nostalgia, along with my childhood memories of cassette tapes and Beanie Babies. I’m terrified that in the not so distant future, clean, fresh air could become something I remember fondly, but rarely have access to. | | But I have hope, too. Working at LCV has shown me that change is always possible when enough people take action for our collective good. My colleagues are brilliant, dedicated, and work tirelessly to protect our democracy and planet. I know the LCV community — staff and members alike — won’t stop fighting for a safe, livable climate, clean water, and clean air — but we have hard work ahead of us. | | I thank you for your support of this important work, and I encourage us all to step outside once in a while for a breath of fresh air... we can’t take this for granted. | | Best, | | Chris Brooks, VP of MembershipLCV | | | | | | | | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. subject: The right to fix our own stuff
body:
| | Peter – When you buy something, it should belong to you. Not the manufacturer.

That’s why Marie just introduced bipartisan legislation to guarantee Americans the right to repair their own electronics, from phones and laptops to washing machines and farm equipment.

Right now, too many manufacturers lock up repair manuals, parts, and tools, forcing families to pay inflated prices or throw things away entirely. It wastes money and time, and it creates mountains of unnecessary e-waste.

Marie has been fighting for this since day one in Congress – whether it’s the REPAIR Act for vehicles, the FARM Act for farmers, or ensuring servicemembers can fix their own equipment. This new bill builds on that work and extends the same principle to everyday electronics.

Research shows families could save hundreds of dollars a year if we pass this into law. But now, Marie needs to know where you stand:
